## Document_1

Carrier aggregation (CA) can drop from a maximum of 5 bands to just 2 bands on Peplink hardware, such as the MAX BR1 5G Pro and MAX BR2 5G Pro, after approximately an hour of use. This behavior has been observed across multiple carriers including Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile, and occurs regardless of whether the CA bands are set to Auto or manually selected. The drop in CA may be influenced by factors such as limitations of the Sierra Wireless modem or Peplink firmware, or external factors related to tower transmission. Stress tests indicate that once the CA drops to 2 bands, it does not increase beyond that level during repeated use.

## Document_2

The Peplink MAX BR1 Pro 5G has been certified for compatibility with AT&T's FirstNet service.

## Document_3

The IMEI number for the Pepwave Max BR1 mini LTEA can be found through InControl2 by clicking on details under the cellular section, as well as directly in the web admin interface under the cellular details on the main page.

## Document_4

To find the IMEI number for the Pepwave Max BR1 Mini LTE-US-T, it can be located on the white sticker inside the original packaging box. Alternatively, the IMEI number can be accessed by logging into the router and navigating to the Cellular Details tab.

## Document_5

The Pepwave MAX Transit Duo requires a high current supply of 2.4 Amps to operate properly on USB power. If using multiple lower current supplies, it is important to utilize both USB connectors to meet the necessary power requirements.

## Document_6

To activate a SIM card for a new BR1 MAX MK2, the IMEI number can be found on the device's box or obtained from the Peplink Partner from whom the device was purchased, as Peplink provides a method for Partners to look up the IMEI by serial number.

## Document_7

An expired warranty on an AP managed by InControl 2 (IC2) does not affect the ability to push configurations to the AP. Users can purchase IC2 subscriptions even after the warranty period has ended to maintain management capabilities.

## Document_8

When using a 24 port switch with two power supplies, it is possible to connect each power supply to a separate UPS battery backup. However, the power usage will not be sequential; instead, it will be load shared, meaning both UPS power sources will be utilized simultaneously rather than one after the other.

## Document_9

To successfully delete a VLAN network that is showing as 'Used by', it is important to check if the VLAN is set as a named VLAN on a specific physical port. Additionally, verify if a SpeedFusion Layer 2 profile is utilizing the VLAN, as this could prevent deletion.

## Document_10

The Peplink Balance 210 supports up to 10,000 concurrent NAT sessions. For detailed specifications, it is advisable to contact a local Peplink partner.

## Document_11

For the Pepwave Max BR1 Mini HW3 variant, a compatible adapter plug for the 4-pin DC power block can be found from Cradlepoint, specifically model 170665-000, which is readily available.

## Document_12

The new Pepwave Max BR1 Mini HW3 variant uses a 4 pin DC power block with a center pin positive configuration for the DC barrel. An adapter plug compatible with this configuration can be found on Amazon, as suggested in the conversation.

## Document_13

To manage access to different SSIDs on a Pepwave Max BR1 5G, you can define a schedule and set that schedule per SSID, allowing you to turn off the personal AP during work hours when the connection is less than ideal.

## Document_14

To connect a Pepwave MAX BR1 Mini Cat 7 to a DC barrel connector, it is advisable to use an adapter rather than cutting or replacing the barrel connector. The power pin-outs for the Molex 4-pin adapter can be found in the user manual, which specifies which pins correspond to DC+ and DC- wires.

## Document_15

The Winegard 360+ antenna system is not suitable for use with the Pepwave Max BR1 Pro 5G due to its insufficient number of antenna elements and its design primarily for 4G/LTE frequencies. It is recommended to use a dedicated 5G antenna, such as the Peplink 42G antenna, which is 5G ready and includes GPS and WiFi capabilities for accessing public WiFi networks.

## Document_16

When attempting to access the login page of a Peplink Max BR1 MK2 router at 192.168.50.1, it is important to verify the IP address assigned to the device connected to the LAN. If the IP address is in the range of 192.168.50.x, users should also check if the HTTPS protocol is required by trying https://192.168.50.1.

## Document_17

To access the login page of a Peplink Max BR1 MK2, if the standard IP address 192.168.50.1 does not respond, it may be necessary to use the reset button located in a small hole on the device to restore functionality.

## Document_18

The Pepwave MAX BR1 router has a default IP address of 192.168.50.1 and uses DHCP to assign IP addresses to connected clients starting from 192.168.50.10. If the SAT TV device is using DHCP, it will receive a new IP address within the 192.168.50.10-100 range. If the SAT TV does not use DHCP, the BR1's network settings can be changed to use the 192.168.1.0/24 network instead of the default 192.168.50.0/24. An advanced IP scanner can be used to identify devices on the network.

## Document_19

If a connection is refused when trying to access a PepLink Max BR1 router at the IP address 192.168.25.1, it is important to verify that the default IP has been changed from 192.168.50.1 to 192.168.25.1. Additionally, checking the IP address of the connected laptop or PC is crucial to ensure it is on the same subnet as the router for successful connectivity.

## Document_20

The Pepwave MAX BR1 Pro does not support converting the WAN port to a LAN port, which means it cannot be configured to provide additional LAN ports beyond the default number available.

## Document_21

In IP passthrough mode, the Pepwave MAX BR1 will retain its default management IP address of 192.168.50.1, but it will not have an IP scheme for routing. To access the BR1 for management, a PC must be assigned a static IP address within the 192.168.50.x subnet. The Linksys router can use its default subnet for DHCP settings to facilitate communication between the devices.

## Document_22

For the MAX HD2 LTE IP67, the power connector part number is ACW-636. Additionally, the PoE injector for this device has a different part number, which is ACW-107.

## Document_23

The default IP address for configuring the Pepwave MAX BR1 router is 192.168.50.1. To access the configuration page wirelessly, one must connect to the built-in access point (AP) of the BR1.

## Document_24

For configuring multiple Pepwave Max BR1 devices, the InControl2 cloud management platform can be used to store configurations in the cloud and push them to all devices, facilitating pre-staging of configurations.

## Document_25

To add users in InControl2, once a person is added, they will receive an email with a unique link. If the email is not received, the user can go to the InControl2 login page and select the 'Reset' option next to 'Forgot your password?' to receive a password reset email by entering their email address and clicking the Send button.

## Document_26

To unregister a router from an InControl2 account, one should remove the device from its current group within the existing organization. After this, the router can be added to a new organization or account.

## Document_27

Currently, InControl 2 (IC2) requires devices to be under warranty for management. If a device goes out of warranty, users must either renew the warranty or purchase an IC2 subscription to continue utilizing the management features. The subscription is considered affordable given the extensive capabilities that IC2 offers.

## Document_28

Carrier aggregation (CA) performance can vary based on the carrier's implementation rather than the limitations of the Peplink hardware or Sierra Wireless modem. In the USA, major carriers like Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile manage CA differently, which can affect the number of bands utilized. The user has observed that while they can achieve up to 5 band CA initially, it tends to drop to 2 bands after about an hour, impacting speeds. The user has not experienced CA dropping below 2 bands, and the response suggests that the carrier's management of CA may be influenced by network conditions and usage patterns.

## Document_29

The Peplink MAX BR1 5G Pro supports band 14, which is used by FirstNet, suggesting potential compatibility with the network. However, it is not explicitly listed on the FirstNet page, so confirmation from Peplink support may be necessary for definitive compatibility information.

## Document_30

The IMEI number for the Pepwave Max BR1 Mini LTE-US-T can be found in two locations: physically on a sticker on the bottom of the unit, where it is labeled after 'IMEA:' followed by a 15-digit number, and digitally through the device's GUI by navigating to Dashboard -> WAN Connection Status -> [name of your connection] -> Details, where it will be listed under 'WAN Connection Status.'

## Document_31

The Pepwave MAX Transit Duo may not operate correctly on 5V USB power if the USB cable is faulty or if the device requires more power due to the installation of two SIM cards and the creation of a tunnel. Insufficient voltage can cause the battery light to flash red every 10 seconds, indicating a power issue.

## Document_32

To activate a SIM card for a BR1 MAX MK2, the IMEI number can be found on the box rather than the device itself. If the admin password is not recognized after changing it, one option is to reset the router using a paperclip, which will allow logging back in. Alternatively, connecting a wired WAN cable and adding the device to InControl2 can bring it online.

## Document_33

Once the warranty of an access point (AP) managed by IC2 expires, new configurations cannot be pushed to the device from IC2. However, the expiration of the warranty does not impact the configurations that have already been applied to the device.

## Document_34

To connect a Pepwave MAX BR1 Mini Cat 7 to a pre-wired DC barrel connector in an Airstream, a specific adapter is required to convert the male barrel connector to a Molex 4-pin. The adapter can be purchased from a specified online retailer in the US.

## Document_35

To access the Sat TV interface after switching to a Max BR1 router, it may be necessary to adjust the IP address settings of the Max BR1 to match the existing network configuration, specifically ensuring it is within the same subnet as the Sat TV device, which is at 192.168.1.11. Additionally, if other devices such as an access point are not accessible, their IP addresses should also be checked to ensure they are correctly configured within the network.

## Document_36

If a connection is refused when trying to access a PepLink Max BR1 router at its IP address 192.168.25.1, one possible cause could be that the web admin port has been changed from the default port 80 to another port. This would result in an inability to connect using the standard URL format.

## Document_37

When attempting to connect to a PepLink Max BR1 router at the IP address 192.168.25.1, users may encounter a 'connection refused' error. Possible causes include incorrect network configuration, such as improper DNS settings or IP address conflicts. In this case, the main DNS was set to the router's IP, which could lead to issues. Additionally, while pinging the router from within the network shows some success, traceroute fails to return results, indicating potential routing issues. SSH connection attempts to port 22 also time out, suggesting that the SSH service may not be running or accessible on the router.

## Document_38

When attempting to connect to a PepLink Max BR1 router at the IP address 192.168.25.1, a connection refused error may occur. This could be due to issues with the router's configuration or network settings. The user is trying to ping the ISP allocated to the cellular modem on the BR1 and aims to remotely access a server on the LAN using SSH. It is noted that public IP addresses are being used on the cellular connection.

## Document_39

The IP address 192.168.25.1 is not accessible from the outside due to being in the 100.64.0.0/10 IP address block, which is used for carrier grade NAT. To access the router from an external network, one can obtain a static public IP address from the carrier or set up a PepVPN or IPSEC connection to a router that has a public IP address.

## Document_40

If a connection is refused when attempting to connect to a PepLink Max BR1 router at the IP address 192.168.25.1, one potential solution is to use the website http://whatsmyrouterip.com/ to help establish a connection through a web browser. This may assist in accessing the router's settings and performing a reset if necessary.

## Document_41

To successfully connect a Pepwave MAX BR1 in bridged mode to a Linksys WRT1900ACS v2 router, it is important to disable IP forwarding on the BR1. After making this change, reboot both devices to allow the Linksys router to obtain the cellular IP address from the BR1.

query: Which diagnostic measures and factors should a technician evaluate when observing a drop on carrier aggregation (CA) bands on a Peplink MAX BR1 5G Pro or BR2 5G Pro with several carriers, and what possible reasons might explain this situation?
answer: When experiencing a drop in carrier aggregation (CA) bands from a maximum of 5 bands to just 2 on Peplink MAX BR1 5G Pro or BR2 5G Pro routers—even after about an hour of use and regardless of whether bands are set to Auto or manual selection—the technician should be aware that this is a known behavior observed across major US carriers (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile). Stress testing shows that once the CA drops to 2 bands, it does not increase again during the session. This reduction in CA is not necessarily due to Peplink firmware or Sierra Wireless modem limitations but may be primarily influenced by how the carrier manages CA in response to network conditions and usage patterns. The drop is not observed to go below 2 bands. Additionally, hardware like the MAX BR1 5G Pro supports relevant bands (e.g., band 14 for FirstNet), but for specific compatibility (such as FirstNet), confirmation with Peplink is advised. Technicians should consider both carrier-side management and hardware/firmware factors in their troubleshooting, but the most likely cause is carrier-specific CA management.

## Document_1

The Peplink Balance 30PRO model includes a Wi-Fi interface, allowing for wireless connections and SSID broadcasting, whereas the Balance 30LTE model does not have a Wi-Fi interface and only supports AP Controller functionality. If the wireless connection is enabled but the SSID is not visible, it is important to confirm the specific model of the Balance 30 being used.

## Document_2

The older Peplink Balance 20 model has a hardware revision that limits its throughput to 100 Mbps, which explains the reduced download speeds observed when the router is connected. In contrast, newer hardware revisions of the Balance 20 can support speeds up to 150 Mbps. Therefore, the performance drop when using the router is likely due to its hardware limitations rather than a configuration issue.

## Document_3

When upgrading from Peplink firmware version 5.1.3 to a later version within the 5.x series, such as 5.3.12 or 5.4.6, an unlock key is not required. Unlock keys are only necessary for major upgrades from firmware 4.x to 5.x. Users should refer to the firmware release notes for additional information before proceeding with the upgrade.

## Document_4

The Peplink Balance 20 has achieved a throughput of 100 Mbps due to both a hardware revision and firmware optimization. This combination has improved its performance capabilities.

## Document_5

To determine the serial number of a device in InControl 2, you need to click on the specific device within your InControl 2 group, where the serial number will be displayed along with other device information.

## Document_6

The Peplink Balance 20 and 30 routers are rated for 100 Mbps of throughput, which includes both upload and download speeds. They support various types of WAN connections, including Ethernet and USB, although some USB connections may require a firmware update. The Balance series is designed to handle multiple WAN connections, ensuring seamless failover in case one connection drops.

## Document_7

The CAT18 cellular module used in the Flexmodule mini for Balance20X and Expansion module for Balance310X is confirmed to be the Telit LM960A18. When comparing the performance of the Telit LM960A18 to the Sierra EM7565 CAT12, users may experience differences in sensitivity and efficiency, particularly in good signal conditions with SINR values between 15-30dB and RSRP values between 75-90dB. Expected gains in upload and download speeds can vary based on these conditions, but specific metrics are not provided in the conversation.

## Document_8

For a Balance 2500 router experiencing a constant high frequency beeping sound, it is suggested that a PSU replacement may be necessary if the router is configured with dual PSUs. The status light on the PSU should be checked, with a normal PSU indicated by a green light. Additionally, the beeping sound can be turned off by pressing the red button located on the rear panel of the Balance 2500.

## Document_9

In a network configuration involving multiple PepLink Balance 305 routers connected to a Balance 508 via IP Sec VPN tunnels to Azure, it is important to ensure that outbound rules are correctly set up for traffic to traverse from the satellite sites to Azure. The Balance 508 needs to properly advertise its routes to the connected 305 devices for successful end-to-end connectivity.

## Document_10

The outbound policy configuration on the PepLink Balance 508 was successfully adjusted, allowing the connected Balance 305 devices to traverse to Azure through the established IP Sec VPN tunnels. This indicates that proper routing and policy settings are essential for enabling connectivity between satellite sites and Azure.

## Document_11

The Peplink Balance 300, which is approximately 15 years old, supports a maximum throughput of 20Mbps. Therefore, if clients are experiencing a maximum speed of 15Mbps, this is within the expected performance limits of the device, despite having three WAN connections with a total potential speed of 300Mbps.

## Document_12

The Balance 50 router's firmware version 6.3 does not currently include preset category blocking pages, which are designed to enhance usability by allowing users to block predetermined categories of objectionable material. These categories are based on a large database and will be updated frequently through InControl2, as well as during new firmware releases.

## Document_13

For the Balance 210 HW4 firmware version 8.0, the sha256 checksum value for the downloaded firmware is b2cace99b7784a5a01c9817907a8c9bffa76607417607d1a4372bc08953a1c40. This checksum was verified by downloading the firmware twice from different ISPs, and both downloads returned the same checksum value, indicating consistency and legitimacy of the file.

## Document_14

Enabling VLANs on a Balance 1350 router does not cause any downtime, allowing for configuration changes without interrupting the network service.

## Document_15

To set up a Point to Point PepLink VPN tunnel between Balance 210-A and Balance 210-C, it is necessary to use custom handshake and data ports for PepVPN on Balance 210-C. These ports must be forwarded through Balance 210-B. The PepVPN profile on Balance 210-A should be configured to connect to the public IP of Balance 210-B using the specified custom ports.

## Document_16

query: What are the differences in technical features, WAN connection capabilities, and maximum throughput among the Peplink Balance 20, Balance 30, and Balance 50, and how might these factors affect users looking to upgrade for faster services such as Starlink?
answer: The Peplink Balance 20 and Balance 30 share the same technical specifications, with the main difference being that the Balance 30 has an extra WAN port, allowing it to support three Ethernet connections compared to two on the Balance 20. Both models also allow one USB 3G/4G connection, which can be set as a backup and can have a bandwidth cap for data management. Their rated throughput is 100 Mbps, and while newer hardware revisions of the Balance 20 can reach up to 150 Mbps, the Balance 50 is similarly rated for a maximum of 100 Mbps throughput. All three models support multi-WAN configurations for failover and a mix of cable, DSL, and cellular connections. However, the Balance 50 is limited to 100 Mbps, which may be insufficient for higher-speed connections like Starlink, which can exceed these speeds. For users seeking to support Starlink or similar high-bandwidth services, the Balance 20X is recommended, as it supports up to 900 Mbps throughput, includes a built-in 4G modem, and can be expanded with additional modules, making it more future-proof for growing network demands.

## Document_1

To configure the GPIO interface on Peplink routers, users can refer to the Router API documentation available from Peplink. The documentation provides commands for querying the status of GPIO pins, although specific commands were not detailed in the conversation. Additionally, there is a possibility to query the power supply input voltage via the API, but further specifics were not provided in the response.

## Document_2

To reset the password on a Peplink device, smaller models typically have a reset button located in a hole that requires a paperclip to access. Larger models may feature an LCD with buttons for resetting.

## Document_3

The maximum MTU sizes supported on Peplink routers are as follows: Wired WAN has a maximum MTU of 1440 bytes, Cellular WAN has 1428 bytes, Mobile Internet supports 1492 bytes, and Wifi WAN has a maximum MTU of 1500 bytes.

## Document_4

The GPS route history for devices using the PepLink API is retained for a period of 1 year.

## Document_5

To change the master and slave roles in a 1+1 Backup High Availability pair without shutting down the master device, the following steps should be followed: First, log into the Master Device and uncheck 'Resume Master Role after Recovery' in the settings under high availability. Then, reboot the Master Device. Next, log into the previously Slave device, which will now assume the master role, and disable sync configuration. Set the preferred HA role as master. After that, log into the previously Master device, which will now be the slave, and set its preferred HA role as slave, entering the serial number of the new master device. Finally, reboot the slave device to complete the process.

## Document_6

The issue of a unit restarting multiple times may be related to changes made to outbound policy rules, particularly when switching the order of WAN connections, such as changing from WAN4 to WAN2. This problem reportedly began after upgrading to the latest firmware, suggesting a potential compatibility or stability issue with the new firmware when modifying outbound policies.

## Document_7

The ports in question are Micro USB ports, not USB-C, and are used solely for powering the device from a power brick during portable testing. These ports are wired only to the DC power bus and do not support data transmission, meaning they cannot be used to connect a Max Adapter or add another cellular modem.

## Document_8

Layer 2 VPN profiles can only include one VLAN or LAN segment on each device, meaning that a single profile cannot be shared across multiple VLANs.

## Document_9

To resolve the issue of a Pepwave device being registered to another organization in InControl, it is necessary to open a support ticket with Peplink. The support team will require a diagnostic report from the device and a picture showing the silver label as proof of ownership.

## Document_10

In the context of DHCP, the process involves DORA (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge), where a client obtains an IP address. During the Discover and Request stages, clients send options to the DHCP server. The Peplink DHCP server will send all configured options during both the Offer and Acknowledge phases. A DHCP NACK (Negative Acknowledgment) is sent by the Peplink DHCP server only if it refuses to lease the requested IP address to the client.

## Document_11

On 24 May 2023, a maintenance fix was deployed to all InControl "planets" simultaneously, leading to an overload of the device communication cluster due to a high volume of incoming report data. This caused devices to initiate re-authentication, but the cluster was unable to process all requests in time, resulting in devices being incorrectly treated as offline. The system ceased requesting report data at 00:30, allowing the cluster load to decrease and re-authentication requests to be processed gradually. By 01:45, all devices were back online. To prevent future occurrences, fixes will be applied to only one planet at a time, additional resources have been added to the communications cluster, and the system will stop identifying devices as offline during high authentication volumes to avoid false alarms.

## Document_12

To delete an organization in InControl that was created with a personal email and is empty of devices, log in using that email, navigate to Organization Settings, and delete all devices on the device management page. The organization will be removed automatically after 28 days.

## Document_13

The InControl 2 Mars and Earth systems will undergo scheduled maintenance on November 14 and 28, 2022, at 00:30 GMT+0, lasting 60 minutes each, during which access to the system, Find My Peplink service, and captive portals may be less responsive or intermittently unavailable. The systems will be upgraded to version 2.12.0. The maintenance for the Earth system has been rescheduled to November 28 due to a potential performance issue identified in the release, and no maintenance was carried out on November 21.

## Document_14

The IC2 platform allows for tracking data usage by IMSI or ICCID per SIM card or across groups of SIMs when using Data pools from MVNOs. Partners have successfully built in-house systems utilizing the IC2 API to extract necessary data for monitoring and reporting purposes.

## Document_15

The InControl 2 Mars system will be upgraded to version 2.9.2 on September 27, 2021, at 00:30 GMT+0, with scheduled maintenance lasting 60 minutes. During this time, access to the system, Find My Peplink service, and captive portals may be less responsive or intermittently unavailable. The WAN quality reports in version 2.9.2 are noted to be easier to read, with improved chart intelligibility and hover functionality.

## Document_16

The InControl Mars and Mercury systems are undergoing scheduled maintenance on June 9, 2021, at 00:30 GMT+0, lasting 60 minutes. During this time, access to the systems and captive portals may be less responsive or intermittently unavailable. The upgrade will merge the Mercury system into Mars, with organizations on Mercury appearing on Mars after the upgrade.

## Document_17

InControl version 2.8.6 was deployed to the Mercury system, during which an issue with PepVPN configuration was identified. However, due to a configuration protection mechanism, no impact was made to any devices. The deployment to the Mars system has been postponed to September 8 at 00:30 GMT+0.

## Document_18

Currently, there is no report available that shows SIM ID, IMEI, and MDN together for data usage. However, there is a SIM data usage export tool under 'Sim Pool Reports' that is IMSI based. Additionally, SIM usage data can be accessed through Peplink's API services, which also operates on an IMSI basis, with endpoints available for hourly, daily, and monthly SIM usages.

## Document_19

Documentation and tutorials for InControl 2, including information on the Ads module and advertisement reports, can be found at the Ad Delivery Service Portal and the Ad Delivery Service Evaluation Guide. These resources provide insights into the capabilities of the Ads module and the types of reports available.

## Document_20

After scheduled maintenance on April 16 at 03:00 GMT+0, some Peplink and Pepwave client units were reported offline in IC2, affecting the Captive Portal functionality. Service was restored at 04:30 GMT+0.

## Document_21

To add users in InControl2, once a person is added, they will receive an email with a unique link. If the email is not received, the user can go to the InControl2 login page and select the 'Reset' option next to 'Forgot your password?' to receive a password reset email by entering their email address and clicking the Send button.

## Document_22

To set up email notifications for WAN connection status on a Peplink Balance, users can navigate to Group > Settings > Notifications to create multiple notification profiles for various purposes. This allows for more reliable notification management compared to using the CE device for sending alerts.

## Document_23

To move a device from one group to another within InControl, navigate to the Group Dashboard page, click on Manage, select the device by ticking the corresponding box, and then use the Actions pull-down menu to select Move.

## Document_24

Currently, InControl 2 (IC2) requires devices to be under warranty for management. If a device goes out of warranty, users must either renew the warranty or purchase an IC2 subscription to continue utilizing the management features. The subscription is considered affordable given the extensive capabilities that IC2 offers.

## Document_25

To query the status of a GPIO pin on Peplink routers, you can use the API endpoint 'https://192.168.50.1/api/status.gpio.input?list', which returns the status including voltage and type of the GPIO pin. For example, the response indicates the voltage level and whether the GPIO is enabled. This allows for monitoring the input voltage of the router.

## Document_26

To change the Master and Slave roles in a 1+1 Backup High Availability pair, the following steps should be followed: log into the Master device and uncheck 'Resume Master Role after Recovery' in the High Availability settings, then reboot the Master device. Next, log into the previously Slave device, disable configuration sync, set its preferred HA role to Master, and then log into the previously Master device to set its preferred HA role to Slave, entering the serial number of the new Master device. Finally, reboot the Slave device. This procedure allows for a successful role change without issues, provided both devices are connected to the same switch.

## Document_27

The Balance 710 HW1 experiences issues where it loses outbound WAN connection upon saving changes made to the unit. This problem occurs not only when changing outbound policies but also when modifications are made in the firewall section and inbound access services section. After applying changes, the unit may restart or fail to accept outbound/inbound WAN connections.

## Document_28

The Peplink BA310v2 experienced spontaneous restarts, which were suspected to be hardware related. After replacing the original power supply unit (PSU) with a different make and model, the reboot issues were resolved. When replacing a PSU, it is crucial to ensure that the voltage is identical, the polarity matches, and that the PSU can supply sufficient power to avoid damage or stability issues.

## Document_29

To inform DHCP clients that they are on a metered connection, one approach involves using DHCP option 43, which can be configured on Peplink routers. Additionally, Windows may utilize vendor extensions to convey network cost information through a specific packet format, where the cost level indicates the type of connection (e.g., unrestricted, fixed, variable) and cost flags provide details about usage conditions (e.g., over data limit, congested, roaming).

## Document_30

In Peplink routers, while it is possible to set various DHCP options, including option 43, there is no configuration option available to force the sending of option 43 in DHCP replies without it being specifically requested by the client. This behavior is noted as potentially necessary for clients to recognize a connection as metered, similar to how Android devices handle metered connections. However, testing indicates that simply setting option 43 does not achieve the desired outcome of clients automatically recognizing the connection as metered, suggesting that a more complex or vendor-specific approach may be required.

## Document_31

On January 2, 2024, the InControl system experienced an issue where many devices were falsely marked as offline due to a system component generating high CPU load on a memory database, which became overloaded. The issue was resolved by 07:12 UTC, with devices gradually appearing online again, and the system was fully recovered by 07:48 UTC.

## Document_32

Following the scheduled maintenance of the InControl 2 Mars system on September 27, 2021, users reported that Device Reports were missing most data on all units, and MediaFast Reports did not function with the SDX Pro.

query: What methods should a technician use to check and analyze the input voltage and GPIO signals on a Peplink router, and what corrective actions are recommended if unstable voltage or unexpected device restarts are detected?
answer: A technician can monitor the power supply input voltage and GPIO status on a Peplink router by using the Router API. The API provides endpoints (such as '/api/status.gpio.input?list') that return the voltage and status (including type and enabled state) of GPIO pins, allowing the technician to check the input voltage remotely. If the router experiences instability or restarts that are suspected to be related to the power supply, the technician should ensure that any replacement power supply matches the required voltage and polarity, and that it can supply sufficient power. Using a power supply with incorrect voltage, polarity, or insufficient current capacity can cause reboot issues or damage the unit. Therefore, proper monitoring and correct PSU selection are both critical for stable operation.

## Document_1

To monitor websites visited by users on a home network using an SDX Pro, one can navigate to the Status -> Active Sessions page, which provides information on connected devices and allows for searching and sorting of active connections.

## Document_2

To address a Peplink device that is stuck on booting up due to suspected Compact Flash corruption, it is suggested to connect to the console port, which may allow the user to boot from a second firmware file.

## Document_3

The Peplink Balance 580 may fail to boot up, which could indicate a hardware issue if it is unresponsive despite the status light being green and the LCD lighting up without displaying any information. In such cases, it is recommended to open a support ticket for further assistance.

## Document_4

In the API response model for the endpoint "/rest/o/{organization_id}/g/{group_id}/d/{device_id}/loc", the parameter "isStatic" is a boolean that indicates whether the location of the device is static. If "isStatic=true", it means the location is defined as a static location on the device detail page or during the device addition process.

## Document_5

The Peplink MediaFast 500 is the successor to the MediaFast 380, which was available for a limited time in early 2014. The current models in the MediaFast series are the 200, 500, and 750.

## Document_6

The Balance 305 may experience hardware failures, particularly after approximately three years of use, leading to issues such as an abnormal LCD display and freezing. A reboot may temporarily restore functionality, but the device can stop working again shortly after. In cases of persistent failure, contacting the vendor may result in recommendations against repair due to warranty expiration, suggesting that replacement might be necessary.

## Document_7

To address an abnormal LCD display issue on a Balance 305, a hard reset can be attempted by unplugging the unit, holding the power button for 10 seconds, and then plugging it back in. If the problem persists, it may be related to thermal issues; reseating the memory and checking the processor heat sink can be beneficial. If the thermal pad is dried up, replacing it with new thermal compound can help restore functionality, although the display issue may remain unresolved until a replacement unit is obtained.

## Document_8

query: What are the ways to track and generate reports on user web activity through an SDX Pro on a home network, and how do the different monitoring techniques compare?
answer: To monitor websites visited by users on a home network with an SDX Pro, you have two main options. First, you can use the SDX Pro's local interface by navigating to the Status -> Active Sessions page, which shows connected devices and allows for searching and sorting of active connections. This method provides real-time session information but does not categorize websites or group them by type. Alternatively, you can enable Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) on the SDX Pro through InControl2. Once DPI is enabled, you can access detailed DPI reports from InControl2, which break down websites visited by category and provide more comprehensive reporting compared to the local interface. Thus, while the Active Sessions page is suitable for quick, real-time monitoring, DPI via InControl2 offers advanced reporting and categorization.

The Peplink Pepwave Surf On-The-Go Wi-Fi Router (SUS-AGN1) can be used to provide internet access via public Wi-Fi or a mobile hotspot to a laptop through an Ethernet cable. The Pepwave Max On The Go (MOTG) is suitable for connecting multiple USB 4G/LTE modems to a laptop for video file transfer; however, it only supports load balancing and does not provide bonding capabilities. For bonding, a Peplink Balance 210 router is recommended, which would be necessary for combining multiple connections effectively in the transmission path.

The Balance One is suggested as a more suitable option for this configuration.

## Document_4

For live video streaming using the Pepwave MAX On-The-Go with SpeedFusion, it is recommended to also have a compatible Peplink Balance device to utilize SpeedFusion bonding technology effectively. While the MAX On-The-Go can function as a load balancer, integrating it with a Peplink Balance on the streaming server side will enable the creation of a bonded connection that combines multiple WANs for improved bandwidth and reliability.

## Document_5

For live video streaming using the Pepwave MAX On-The-Go with SpeedFusion, it is important to prioritize RTP over IP using Quality of Service (QoS) settings. A QoS application rule should be added on both the streaming device and the server side, specifying 'Audio Video Streaming' and 'RTP' as the application to ensure optimal performance during streaming.

## Document_6

For live video streaming using the Pepwave MAX On-The-Go with SpeedFusion, it is important to configure Quality of Service (QoS) settings. This can be done in the Balance under Network > QoS > Application and on the MAX OTG under Advanced > QoS > Application. The supported application category for streaming is 'Audio Video Streaming' with the application set to 'RTP'. Additionally, custom applications can be added for prioritization using DSCP values.

## Document_7

When using the Pepwave MAX On-The-Go with SpeedFusion for live video streaming, it is important to consider the quality of the connections being bonded. It is recommended to use connections with similar latency and throughput for optimal performance. If bonding a high latency VSAT connection with a low latency fiber connection, it is advisable to set the fiber connection as priority 1 and the VSAT as priority 2 in the SpeedFusion profile to ensure traffic primarily routes through the fiber connection while allowing for real-time failover to the VSAT connection, creating an 'Unbreakable' connection.

query: What methods enable stable, high-throughput live video broadcasts from a mobile camera team utilizing several 3G/4G LTE networks, and which essential SpeedFusion bonding configurations and key considerations are required when using Pepwave MAX On-The-Go together with Peplink Balance hardware?
answer:
To achieve reliable, high-bandwidth live video streaming from a mobile camera crew using multiple 3G/4G LTE connections, deploy a Pepwave MAX On-The-Go router equipped with multiple USB 3G/4G LTE modems. Use SpeedFusion bonding technology to combine the bandwidth of these connections. The MAX On-The-Go sends the video stream via a SpeedFusion VPN tunnel to a Peplink Balance device (such as Balance 380) at the broadcaster’s media server location or data center, which then connects to the streaming platform via a landline.

Critical configuration steps include:
1. Configure SpeedFusion bonding between the MAX On-The-Go and the Balance device. On the MAX On-The-Go, define the remote IP, remote ID, and password for the SpeedFusion server (Balance or FusionHub); the remote server sets the password and local ID.
2. Prioritize audio and video traffic using QoS settings on both the MAX On-The-Go (Advanced > QoS > Application) and the Balance device (Network > QoS > Application), specifying ‘Audio Video Streaming’ and ‘RTP’ for optimal streaming performance.
3. Use WAN connections with similar latency and throughput for best bonding performance; if mixing high-latency (e.g., VSAT) and low-latency (e.g., fiber) connections, prioritize the lower-latency link in the SpeedFusion profile for primary routing, with the higher-latency link as failover.
4. Adjust MTU and UDP packet sizes as needed to avoid packet loss, e.g., set WAN1 MTU to 1300 and keep UDP packets at or below 1200 bytes.
5. Consider using MAX routers with built-in modems for reliability over long durations, as USB dongles may encounter issues in extended use.

Additionally, firmware enhancements (e.g., latency cut off and packet loss pull back) and features like WAN Smoothing are available to further improve reliability and performance over cellular links. For best results, consult the SpeedFusion best practice handbook.

query: What steps should a technician take to fix and avoid LAN-WAN IP conflicts on Peplink Balance routers, including suggested subnet configurations and procedures for restoring access to the web admin interface if an IP conflict makes it unreachable?
answer: To resolve and prevent LAN-WAN IP address conflicts on Peplink Balance routers, ensure that the LAN and WAN interfaces are assigned to different subnets. For example, set the LAN to 192.168.2.1 if a WAN uses 192.168.1.x. This separation avoids routing confusion and enables proper router functionality. If the web admin interface is inaccessible and an IP conflict is suspected, check the assigned WAN IP (especially if set to DHCP) and change the LAN IP to a unique subnet. After making changes, update DHCP settings and, if necessary, reprogram static IPs on client devices. If still unable to access the admin page, attempt to access the router at its default IP (192.168.1.1) after a reset, and use tools like ping to confirm connectivity. In some cases, using InControl2's Remote Web Admin or performing a factory reset may be necessary to regain access.

citations.claim: LAN and WAN interfaces must be on separate subnets to avoid conflicts; for example, set LAN to 192.168.2.1 if WAN uses 192.168.1.x.
If the web admin interface is inaccessible, check the assigned WAN IP and ensure it does not overlap with the LAN subnet; change LAN IP if needed.
After changing the LAN IP, update DHCP settings and reprogram static IPs on devices if necessary to match the new subnet.
If still unable to access the admin page, try accessing the router at its default IP (192.168.1.1) after a reset and use ping to verify connectivity.
Remote access via InControl2's Remote Web Admin or a factory reset may be used to regain access if standard methods fail.

query: In what ways can a network administrator utilize Peplink or Pepwave equipment to detect and restrict BitTorrent usage on a network, and which settings or functionalities influence the visibility and management of individual user activity?
answer: A network administrator can use Peplink/Pepwave devices to monitor network activity by viewing the MAC addresses of connected users, which is accessible via the Status > Active Sessions section on devices like the Peplink ONE. BitTorrent traffic can be blocked using the Content Blocking feature or by following available guides for blocking such traffic. However, the ability to see individual users and their MAC addresses depends on the network configuration: if the device is set up in station (Bridge) mode, the administrator can see the individual IP and MAC addresses of each user. In contrast, if the device is in routed (NAT) mode, only the WAN-side IP and MAC of the upstream device will be visible, limiting user-level visibility. For setups involving devices like the Ubiquiti Nano Station, adding its MAC address to the Peplink controller may be necessary for monitoring and management. These monitoring and content blocking capabilities help ensure fair usage, reduce bandwidth consumption, and demonstrate compliance with legal requirements.

## Document_1

To create a VPN connection between two Peplink units, such as the BPL 305 and BPL 310, it is important to refer to the user manual for detailed instructions. Additionally, if there is a router or firewall in front of the Peplink devices, port forwarding must be configured for the default protocols TCP 32015 and UDP 4500 to ensure proper connectivity.

## Document_2

To create a VPN connection between two Peplink units, specifically the BPL 305 and BPL 310, users can refer to the Balance and MediaFast User Manual for Firmware 7, which is available for download on the Peplink website under the Support section.

## Document_3

The Max HotSpot supports Virtual WAN (VWAN) as it is compatible with firmware version 8.3, which includes this feature.

## Document_4

Peplink devices currently have limited IPv6 support, primarily allowing basic pass-through of IPv6 traffic from the WAN to the LAN without advanced configuration options. Users can enable IPv6 support on the WAN side, but there is no control over IPv6 traffic routing, LAN configuration, or firewall settings. Additionally, PepVPN does not support native IPv6. While enabling IPv6 may allow devices to access it, this can lead to issues where devices prefer IPv6 over IPv4, potentially bypassing Peplink's traffic control features for services like Google and Netflix.

## Document_5

The Peplink Balance 380 supports up to 50 L2TP users in a VPN Site-Client scheme, while the Balance 710 supports up to 200 L2TP users.

## Document_6

The Peplink B-380 with firmware version 8.0.1 has implemented features that may resolve issues related to establishing GRE tunnels when a Peplink device is included in the network. The previous configuration required for GRE tunnels may no longer be necessary with this updated firmware.

## Document_7

For load balancing with different WAN technologies such as DSL, Fiber, and Vsat, with a throughput requirement of more than 2GB, the Peplink BPL-710 or BPL-1350 Max models are suitable options. These models support NAT for all WAN ports and can reroute traffic from a congested or failed link to other WAN links with different NAT configurations. However, specific information regarding failover for WAN links and NAT resolution for users when one of the WAN links goes down is not provided.

## Document_8

For Peplink B2500, NAT loopback functionality is available without requiring additional configuration, provided that proper inbound NAT rules are defined. This allows devices on the local network to access services using the public IP address of the router.

## Document_9

Peplink devices support IPv6 passthrough, which can be enabled in the WAN settings. For this feature to work, the WAN router must respond to Stateless Address Autoconfiguration advertisements and DHCPv6 requests. IPv6 clients on the LAN will obtain their IPv6 addresses, gateway, and DNS server addresses from the router, and the device will also acquire an IPv6 address for ping/traceroute checks and web admin access.

## Document_10

Peplink devices support IPv6 in pass-through mode, which allows IPv6 traffic to pass from the LAN to the WAN. However, Peplink does not handle IP address assignment or routing for IPv6; this must be managed by the IPv6 device connected to the WAN.

## Document_11

For a High Availability (HA) setup with Peplink routers, it is necessary to use the same model for the failover configuration. This means that a BPL-380 or BPL-580 should not be paired with a smaller model like the BPL-210 for failover purposes.

## Document_12

The Balance routers BPL-310, BPL-380, and BPL-580 are supported by InControl2, allowing for remote management. To manage these routers remotely, it is necessary to register them in InControl2 and ensure that the WAN connection method is correctly configured using default settings for optimal functionality.

## Document_13

The Peplink BPL 210 and BPL 30 can establish a site-to-site VPN, indicated by a green VPN icon, allowing successful pings between the routers' LAN IPs. However, issues arise when attempting to ping hosts within the respective networks, suggesting potential configuration problems related to LAN subnets, VLANs, or WAN connections.

## Document_14

To resolve issues with pinging hosts across a site-to-site VPN between two Peplink devices (BPL 210 and BPL 30), it is necessary to adjust the firewall settings. By default, the firewall may block traffic, so an inbound rule should be added to allow traffic from the LAN (e.g., 192.168.0.0/24) to any destination. This rule needs to be configured on both devices to enable communication between the networks.

## Document_15

When using a Peplink B580 for load balancing in a WISP setup, issues with IPTV may arise, particularly with the RTP protocol. The user reports that IPTV worked well with a previous TP-Link balancer under the same configuration, suggesting that the Peplink device may be interfering with RTP traffic, which is essential for IPTV functionality. The setup involves routing internet through the Peplink B580 to the IPTV service, but it fails to function correctly.

## Document_16

To issue public IPs to clients using a Peplink router, it is important to configure the router to allow the billing gateway to handle 1:1 NAT. If the internet fails on WAN1, the public IPs on the LAN will NAT to the public IPs on WAN2. However, IP forwarding cannot be used on more than one WAN with public IPs. Load balancing and failover can be managed through outbound policy rules in the Peplink Balance router.

## Document_17

To address the issue of not being able to view Active Sessions on a PepLink 310 after a hard reboot, it is recommended to ensure that the device is running the most current firmware version 5.4.9. If the problem persists, opening a support ticket with Peplink is advisable for further assistance. Additionally, if Internet Explorer is being used as the web browser, switching to Firefox or Chrome may resolve the issue.

## Document_18

The Peplink Balance models and Pepwave MAX 700 support IPv6 on a single Ethernet WAN port. When IPv6 support is enabled on a WAN, the WAN router must respond to Stateless Address Autoconfiguration advertisements and DHCPv6 requests. IPv6 clients on the LAN side will obtain their IPv6 address, gateway, and DNS server addresses from the router, which will also acquire an IPv6 address for ping/traceroute checks and web admin access.

## Document_19

Peplink devices have supported IPv6 since firmware version 5.4. The current implementation allows IPv6 support on one of the Ethernet WAN ports, requiring the connected router to respond to Stateless Address Auto Configuration advertisements and DHCPv6 requests. IPv6 clients on the Peplink LAN can acquire their IPv6 addresses, gateway, and DNS server addresses from the WAN. Additionally, the device can obtain an IPv6 address for ping/traceroute checks and web admin access. For devices out of warranty, users can upgrade to the latest firmware for IPv6 support by contacting their local distributor or Peplink directly to discuss warranty extension options if the device is in good condition.

## Document_20

Peplink devices that have an embedded cellular modem support IPv6 WAN IP with cellular service providers, allowing users to utilize IPv6 addresses for their internet connectivity needs.

## Document_21

Peplink routers currently have limited support for IPv6, specifically on Balance-series routers where IPv6 can be enabled under Network>WAN settings. This allows the router to respond to Stateless Address Autoconfiguration advertisements and DHCPv6 requests, enabling IPv6 clients on the LAN to acquire necessary addresses. However, this feature is not available on non-Balance routers like the MAX-series BR1. Future firmware updates, specifically version 9, are expected to improve IPv6 support.

## Document_22

When using a Peplink Balance 20X with Starlink, enabling IPv6 support in the WAN configuration may lead to MAC address conflicts, as experienced by some users. In one case, the conflicts were resolved by completely disabling IPv6, which was initially running with default settings. After disabling IPv6, the issue did not return for over a month.

## Document_23

To configure a Peplink router to issue public IPs to clients, the upstream provider must route a network of public IPs to the Peplink device, which should be set with a public IP address on WAN1 and a /30 subnet mask. The Peplink's LAN must also be in the public IP network, using one of the public IPs for its LAN interface. The DHCP server on the Peplink can then distribute the remaining public IP addresses to the billing gateway. Enabling IP forwarding on WAN1 ensures that public IP addresses from the billing gateway are sent out without NAT, maintaining their original public IPs, while traffic going out through other WANs will be NATed.

## Document_24

Peplink devices currently do not fully support IPv6, and the implementation of full support will occur in phases. Users are advised to continue using IPv4 addresses for the time being.

## Document_25

To configure a Gateway/Router, specifically the BR1, for dual stack operation with T-Mobile Internet at Home, it is possible to set up the WAN link to use IPv6 while having the capability to fail back to IPv4 if issues arise. There is a mention of T-Mobile being able to announce a /64 IPv6 Prefix, which could be beneficial for the configuration.

query: What restrictions and setup prerequisites exist for IPv6 functionality on Peplink Balance-series routers, and in what ways do these impact addressing and traffic management on WAN and LAN interfaces?
answer: Peplink Balance-series routers support IPv6 in pass-through mode on a single Ethernet WAN port. For IPv6 to work, the connected WAN router must respond to Stateless Address Autoconfiguration advertisements and DHCPv6 requests, allowing IPv6 clients on the LAN to receive their IPv6 addresses, gateway, and DNS servers from the WAN. The Peplink device can also acquire an IPv6 address for its web admin access and for ping/traceroute checks. However, Peplink does not handle IPv6 address assignment or routing—this must be managed by the upstream device. There is no advanced IPv6 configuration for LAN, firewall, or routing, and PepVPN does not support native IPv6. This means devices may prefer IPv6 and bypass Peplink’s traffic control features, potentially leading to issues with services like Google or Netflix. IPv6 support is not available on non-Balance routers like the MAX-series BR1, though future firmware may expand support. Full IPv6 support is planned for phased implementation, so users are advised to continue using IPv4 for now if they require advanced routing or firewall control.

query: What configuration steps should a technician take to optimize real-time app performance, such as Zoom and Teams, by utilizing Peplink's SpeedFusion technology, outbound policy settings, and WAN smoothing while bonding Starlink and 5G links, and what important factors related to latency, packet loss, and session persistence need attention during this process?
answer: To optimize real-time applications like Zoom and Teams when bonding Starlink and 5G connections using Peplink's SpeedFusion, configure SpeedFusion tunnels that bond both connections and enable WAN smoothing. WAN smoothing reduces latency and packet loss by duplicating packets across both links, ensuring higher reliability for real-time voice and video. Outbound policies should prioritize traffic for these applications through the SpeedFusion tunnels, ensuring critical traffic uses the most reliable path. Technicians should be aware of Starlink's typical packet loss (around 1%) and higher latency compared to 5G; WAN smoothing and Forward Error Correction (FEC) helps mitigate these issues. Session persistence is maintained during failover when using SpeedFusion, so calls and video streams remain active even if one connection drops. It is important to set the MTU to 1500 and use frequent health checks to stabilize Starlink links. Technicians should also be mindful that overall latency in a bonded connection is determined by the slowest link (often Starlink), so performance tuning may involve adjusting which applications use the bonded tunnel versus direct 5G. Lastly, proper naming of WAN connections and careful management of SpeedFusion overhead (about 18%) are important for optimal configuration and troubleshooting.

## Document_1

The logs indicate multiple authentication failures for the SSID 'Audhumbla', with the reason for disconnection being 'CONN_FAILED'. The clients experience temporary disconnection from the WiFi network, which suggests issues with authentication. The network is configured with WPA2-Personal security and operates on the 802.11n standard with a channel set to 11 and 100% power output. The presence of auth_failures in the logs suggests that the clients may be having trouble authenticating with the network, potentially due to configuration issues or compatibility problems with the clients' connection methods.

## Document_2

To reset the username and password for the Pepwave Surf Soho mk3 without losing the current configuration, the reset will set the admin username and password to 'admin/admin', change the web admin port to 80/443, and restrict web admin access to the LAN only.

## Document_3

The Pepwave Surf SOHO mk3 router does not support IPv6 passthrough according to its product specifications, meaning IPv6 traffic is not allowed by default. Some users prefer this lack of IPv6 support as it can help prevent VPN leaks and reduce potential issues, as fewer features can lead to a lower attack surface.

## Document_4

In firmware version 7.0.1 of the Pepwave Soho 3, VLAN functionality was included, but it appears to have been removed in subsequent versions. The router also has a security feature that temporarily blocks any IP address with too many failed login attempts.

## Document_5

To resolve authentication issues with a PEPWAVE_SOHO Wi-Fi network, ensure that the Wi-Fi AP is set to WPA/WPA2 Personal and that the correct password is applied. After saving the changes, the client device should connect using the SOHO SSID and the specified password. Additionally, it is recommended to check that the device is running the latest firmware version 6.2.0 for optimal performance.

## Document_6

To address freezing issues with the Pepwave SURF_SOHO_612A, it is important to ensure that the router is running the latest firmware version. If the freezing problem continues after updating to the latest firmware, it is recommended to submit a support ticket for further assistance.

## Document_7

A Pepwave Soho can connect to two Pepwave Sohos via VPN.

## Document_8

To resolve issues with a PepWave Surf OTG not obtaining an IP address via DHCP from a Verizon Jetpack MiFi 6620L, performing a factory reset on the Surf OTG is recommended. If the problem persists, opening a support ticket for further investigation may be necessary.

## Document_9

To transfer settings from an old Balance 380 to a new one, swapping the card is not possible. However, if InControl was used, the device configuration is automatically backed up to the cloud with every change, allowing for easy download of the settings from there.

## Document_10

The IMEI of a cellular device can be found in the Dashboard of the Pepwave router by clicking on the "Details" link for the Cellular connection, which displays the IMEI in a pop-up window.

## Document_11

The main difference between the Peplink Balance One and the Balance One Core is that the Balance One includes Wi-Fi capabilities, whereas the Balance One Core does not have Wi-Fi functionality.

## Document_12

The Balance One is not affected by the KRACK WPA2 Vulnerability, which only impacts devices with WiFi WAN capabilities.

## Document_13

Aggregating four SIM cards to achieve a total speed of 80 Mbps is not feasible due to the inherent challenges in bonding cellular connections. For more detailed information on this topic, refer to resources provided by Peplink distributors, which discuss the limitations of SpeedFusion technology in cellular bonding.

## Document_14

To configure a Pepwave Soho Mk3 to act as a simple switch and allow connected devices to receive IP addresses from the ISP's LTE router in the 192.168.1.x range, DHCP should be turned off on the Soho. The DHCP should be enabled on the ISP router, and the ISP router/modem should be connected to the Soho's LAN port. Additionally, the Soho should be assigned an IP address within the same subnet as the ISP router but outside of its DHCP range.

## Document_15

The Pepwave Soho MK3 does not support IPv6, which may raise concerns about online security, particularly for users whose ISPs, like Comcast, utilize IPv6. The MK3 functions primarily as a basic firewall and does not provide advanced security features such as Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) or Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS). Users should be aware that while the MK3 can perform basic filtering, it is not designed to be a comprehensive security appliance.

## Document_16

The Pepwave Surf Soho Mk3 does not support wireless meshing with another Surf Soho Mk3; it can only function as an uplink for the Pepwave AP One. Therefore, to achieve a meshed network setup, one should consider replacing the second Surf Soho Mk3 with a Pepwave AP One to enable the desired functionality of broadcasting the same network across both devices.

## Document_17

If a PepWave SURF SOHO MK3 is experiencing issues with WiFi connectivity and the reset button is unresponsive, accessing the device through InControl2 may provide a solution. Users can add the device to InControl2 for management and troubleshooting purposes.

## Document_18

The Pepwave Surf SOHO Mk3 does not support IPv6 passthrough, meaning that IPv6 traffic is not allowed by default. Therefore, it is possible to block IPv6 traffic wholly or in part using this device.

## Document_19

The Pepwave Surf SOHO MK3 does not support IPv6 pass-through mode, which explains the absence of the option to enable IPv6 on the WAN port. The user manual will be updated to clarify this feature for the Surf SOHO MK3.

## Document_20

The Pepwave Surf OTG will receive updates to protect it from the KRACK vulnerability, which was announced in October 2017.

## Document_21

To change the WAN priority list in the Peplink Surf SOHO Mk3 using the Router Utility iOS app, you can drag the WAN interface to the desired priority position.

## Document_22

The System Time displayed in the Admin Dashboard and Status panels of the PepWave Surf On-The-Go (version 1.0.21) is hardcoded and cannot be changed by the user.

## Document_23

On a Pepwave UBR router, only a single Wi-Fi as WAN connection can be active at any given moment, although multiple Wi-Fi as WAN profiles can be configured for use.

## Document_24

To address the issue of seeing the hotspot `PEPWAVE_XXXX`, one can disable the Access Point feature or rename the Wi-Fi Access Point to a preferred name.

## Document_25

Wi-Fi meshing is a technology that allows for the extension of Wi-Fi coverage wirelessly, enabling seamless roaming between access points (APs) without the need for Ethernet cables. While traditional setups involve hardwired connections between APs for optimal performance, meshing provides flexibility in scenarios where running cables is impractical or too costly. Peplink supports both Wi-Fi meshing and roaming, allowing users to configure multiple APs to work together either through wired connections or wirelessly. The setup process for meshing can be done via the Peplink user interface or through InControl for zero-touch configuration. Users must create a wireless mesh network and assign it to a profile to ensure proper functionality. The technology also includes considerations for performance limitations, emphasizing that wired connections are preferable when possible.

## Document_26

The log indicates that clients are experiencing authentication failures with the SSID 'Audhumbla', leading to temporary disconnections. The reason code 2 signifies that the previous authentication is no longer valid, which may point to client configuration issues or unsupported features by the clients. It is suggested to check if the configuration has worked reliably on older firmware versions, test clients against another access point with identical settings, and consider disabling WPA3 if enabled, as well as turning off features like PMF (802.11w) or other extensions such as 802.11k/r/v that may be causing connectivity issues.

## Document_27

To regain access to a Soho mk3 router after losing the username and password, users can utilize the Remote Web Admin feature through the InControl2 central management platform. If InControl2 is not available, a factory reset is necessary, which will erase all current configurations on the router.

## Document_28

To reset the username and password for a Soho mk3 router without losing the current configuration, access the device dashboard in InControl2 and navigate to the settings for remote web admin.

## Document_29

To resolve authentication issues with the PEPWAVE_SOHO Wi-Fi network, ensure that the security policy is set to WPA/WPA2 - Personal in the security settings. Additionally, reset the wireless SSID pre-shared key and delete any related Wi-Fi profiles on the mobile device before re-associating with the Surf Soho Wi-Fi access point.

## Document_30

To import settings from an old Peplink Balance 380 to a new one, it is essential to have a backup of the configuration file, which can be downloaded from the router's admin interface under System > Configuration > Download Active Configurations. If a backup is available, it can be imported into the new device. However, swapping the internal card between devices is not a viable option. Regularly backing up the configuration after changes is recommended for ease of recovery.

## Document_31

Swapping the card from an old Balance 380 to a new Balance 380 is a viable method to transfer settings, and it successfully powered on and functioned correctly. However, it is necessary to upgrade the firmware from version 5.4 to a newer version for optimal performance.

## Document_32

To transfer settings from an old Peplink Balance 380 to a new one, it is possible to back up the configuration file from the old device and then import it into the new device.

## Document_33

Aggregating multiple SIM cards in a Pepwave HD4 router can potentially increase overall bandwidth, but actual speeds may be limited by the bandwidth pool of the cellular tower being used. The performance can vary depending on the provider and the specific tower's capacity. While the theoretical expectation is to achieve higher speeds by using multiple SIMs, practical limitations may prevent reaching the desired aggregate speed due to network constraints.

## Document_34

To aggregate the speed of multiple SIM cards using Pepwave MAX HD2 or HD4 models, it is important to choose suitable frequency-specific antennas and align narrow beam width directional antennas towards different towers. Splitting SIMs across multiple carriers is recommended, ensuring they are not part of a Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO). Conducting detailed surveys of the area, including carrier back-haul and population density, is crucial. Additionally, utilizing the latest firmware features to select specific frequencies for each SIM can enhance performance.

## Document_35

The Pepwave MAX series includes LTE-A models that can combine multiple frequency bands to enhance speed. To achieve bandwidth bonding with models like the Pepwave MAX-HD2 LTE-A or HD4 LTE-A, it is necessary to utilize both primary and secondary signal strengths from multiple SIM cards to aggregate their speeds effectively.

## Document_36

To achieve an aggregated speed of 80 Mbps using four SIM cards in a router with four slots, it is necessary to utilize a device that supports such aggregation, like the Pepwave HD4. The Load-Balance feature can be used for distributing traffic across multiple connections, but it may require routing adjustments if users are behind a NAT, depending on the specific network configuration.

## Document_37

To achieve speed aggregation from multiple SIM cards in a Pepwave device, it is feasible to aggregate 4 SIMs to potentially reach a combined speed of 80 Mbps. However, specific details on the implementation or configuration steps were not provided in the response.

To mesh two PepLink Surf SOHO Mk3 routers wirelessly and broadcast the same network, the first Surf SOHO can create two SSIDs: "Network1" and "AcrossTheStreet". The second Surf SOHO should then use WiFi as WAN connected to the "AcrossTheStreet" network, allowing it to also broadcast "Network1". It is recommended to limit the "AcrossTheStreet" network to one frequency band, using 2.4GHz for better range over longer distances or 5GHz for faster speeds and reduced interference over shorter distances.

query: What actions should a technician take to resolve ongoing WiFi authentication issues on a Pepwave Surf Soho Mk3 network configured with WPA2-Personal, and what recommendations apply to both firmware updates and client device configurations?
answer: To troubleshoot persistent WiFi authentication failures on a Pepwave Surf Soho Mk3 network configured with WPA2-Personal, the technician should first ensure that the WiFi security setting is explicitly set to WPA/WPA2-Personal and that the correct pre-shared key is applied on both the router and client devices. If issues persist, reset the wireless SSID pre-shared key and delete any saved WiFi profiles on the affected client devices before reconnecting. The technician should also verify that the router is running the latest compatible firmware (at least version 6.2.0 or newer), as older firmware may have unresolved compatibility or stability issues. If authentication failures continue, check client device compatibility with WPA2 and consider disabling advanced features such as WPA3, PMF (802.11w), or 802.11k/r/v extensions on the AP, as these may cause connectivity problems. Testing with another access point configured identically can help isolate whether the issue is specific to the Soho Mk3 or the client devices.

query: What procedures and factors should be addressed when creating a VPN link to a designated VLAN on a Peplink Balance router, and in what ways do firmware versions and routing capabilities influence this setup?
answer: To establish a VPN connection to a specific VLAN on a Peplink Balance router, start by ensuring that the VLAN is properly configured in the router's settings. Inter-VLAN routing must be enabled in the Network Settings for each VLAN you want accessible via VPN. Make sure there are no Deny rules in the Internal Firewall that could block this connectivity. By default, routes learned through OSPF will allow access to VLANs across the VPN; if access is unavailable, manually add a local static route for the VLAN network to the routing table. The ability to route VPN connections to specific VLANs requires firmware version 7.0.0 or later—earlier versions, such as those supported by Balance 380 HW5, do not support this feature, so users should verify their device’s firmware compatibility on the Peplink website.

query: What systematic, evidence-based troubleshooting procedures should a technician implement to fix a Pepwave MAX BR1 Mini that remains on 'Obtaining IP Address' with an AT&T SIM card (which functions correctly in another device), specifically taking into account APN configurations, firmware version, SIM card compatibility, and device settings?
answer:
To resolve a Pepwave MAX BR1 Mini stuck on 'Obtaining IP Address' with an AT&T SIM (which works in another device), the technician should:

1. Verify the SIM card and plan are active, appropriate, and permitted for use in routers, not just phones, as some phone SIMs or plans are incompatible with routers (Documents 20, 27, 28, 29, 30, 37).
2. Check and explicitly set the APN to the correct value for the AT&T plan (often 'broadband', 'phone', or 'nxtgenphone' depending on SIM type and plan), and avoid the 'auto' setting (Documents 1, 5, 14, 18, 19, 27, 39).
3. Ensure the device is running the latest firmware, as updates often resolve cellular connectivity issues (Documents 1, 4, 12, 15, 17, 24, 27, 38, 39).
4. Adjust device settings: Try changing Network Mode between 'Auto', 'Generic', and 'AT&T Only'; toggle between LTE/3G/Auto; and consider switching Operator settings between 'Auto' and 'Custom' (Documents 6, 12, 15, 16, 32).
5. If the issue persists, test the SIM in another device to confirm it is not defective, and test a known-good SIM in the BR1 Mini to check for device-specific issues (Documents 8, 9, 16, 22).
6. If all above steps fail, generate a diagnostic report and contact Peplink support, enabling Remote Assistance if possible (Documents 7, 17, 20).

Note: Signal strength alone does not guarantee connectivity; configuration must match carrier requirements (Document 39).

Update the device to the latest firmware to resolve known connectivity issues.

query: What methods allow a technician to establish secure and dependable remote access from the public internet to a device located behind a Pepwave MAX BR1 Mini with only a private (carrier NAT) cellular WAN IP address?
answer: A technician can achieve secure and reliable remote access to a device behind a Pepwave MAX BR1 Mini with a private (carrier NAT) cellular WAN IP by deploying a FusionHub virtual appliance on a public cloud service (such as AWS or Vultr), which provides a public IP address. The MAX BR1 Mini should establish a PepVPN tunnel to the FusionHub. Once the tunnel is active, remote access can be established in two main ways: (1) configuring port forwarding on the FusionHub from its public IP to the device's LAN IP behind the BR1, or (2) using the FusionHub as a VPN server (e.g., with L2TP over IPSEC or OpenVPN), allowing remote clients to connect to the FusionHub and securely reach devices on the BR1's LAN. Proper routing and VPN security settings (such as MS-CHAP v2 for L2TP/IPSEC) must be configured, and troubleshooting may be needed to ensure that VPN clients can reach the BR1's LAN IPs. This solution avoids the limitations of carrier NAT and does not require a static or public IP on the BR1 itself.

query: What steps should a technician follow to set up a Pepwave Max Transit with Firmware 7 for optimal use of both Wi-Fi-as-WAN and Wi-Fi AP features, maintaining dual-band support and load balancing, and which troubleshooting methods can resolve problems with SSID visibility?
answer: A technician should first configure two Wi-Fi-as-WAN connections (one for 2.4GHz and one for 5GHz) through the Dashboard, ensuring both are set to Priority 1 in the WAN Connection Status for simultaneous use and load balancing. This dual-band setup enables the router to use both Wi-Fi bands as WAN sources. Next, create a Wi-Fi AP by defining a new SSID, setting appropriate security, and configuring it to operate on both 2.4GHz and 5GHz for optimal local connectivity. If issues arise with SSID broadcasting (e.g., 5G Wi-Fi not broadcasting), disable the 2.4G WAN to check for channel interference, use a Wi-Fi analyzer to select a less congested channel, and consider manually setting the AP channel before reverting to auto mode. Ensure Auto Channel Update is enabled and set to check every hour. If problems persist, a device reset or temporarily disabling the 2.4G WAN may help resolve interference and broadcasting issues.
