Peplink Balance devices, specifically models 210 and above, support High Availability (HA) failover using Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP). In an HA setup, periodic VRRP advertisement packets are sent from the master device to specific IP multicast addresses, allowing the slave device to take over if the master fails. The virtual IP (VIP) serves as the default gateway for LAN devices, and both master and slave units must be on the same subnet with a unique HA group identifier. Configuration Sync can be enabled for the slave to automatically apply changes from the master every five minutes, but this locks the slave's web admin interface until disabled. Failover typically occurs within 10-15 seconds, and both devices must be connected to the internet in the same mode, either NAT or Drop-in mode, with the VIP set as the default gateway for LAN hosts.

query: What are the essential configuration steps and prerequisites for achieving smooth failover in a Peplink Balance HA deployment using VRRP, and which frequent mistakes should technicians be wary of, particularly with respect to device synchronization and network design?
answer: To ensure seamless failover in a Peplink Balance High Availability (HA) setup using VRRP, both routers must be configured in a master-slave (active-standby) architecture, where one device is designated as the master and the other as the slave. Both devices must be on the same subnet, share the same HA group identifier, and use the same operational mode (either NAT or Drop-in). The Virtual IP (VIP) must be set as the default gateway for all LAN hosts. Configuration Sync can be enabled for the slave to automatically inherit settings from the master (with sync intervals such as every five minutes), or the slave can be configured manually. During normal operation, the master sends periodic VRRP advertisement packets to a multicast address; if these are not received by the slave within 10-15 seconds (the typical failover window), the slave takes over, re-establishes WAN connections, and binds the VIP for LAN connectivity. Upon recovery, the master resumes its role. Use additional Ethernet switches to avoid single points of failure in the network topology. A common pitfall is failing to synchronize configurations, which can result in mismatched settings and failed failover. Another is not ensuring both devices are on the same subnet or not using the same HA group identifier. Technicians should also avoid using peer-to-peer HA topologies, as Peplink's HA implementation only supports master-slave operation. In some cases, issues can arise if the VRRP MAC address is not correctly set or if both routers attempt to assume the master role, especially after connectivity disruptions; careful diagnostics and physical connection checks are recommended to resolve such issues.

To configure band selection on a Pepwave BR1 Mini, it is possible to use two SIM cards from the same carrier. The MAX Adapter 5G is incompatible with the MAX BR1 Pro 5G, as it is designed for devices with a USB WAN port and requires firmware version 8.1.1 or higher for compatible devices. The Pepwave MAX BR1 Pro 5G has a single modem, which means it can only use one SIM card at a time for cellular connectivity. Although it can accept a second SIM card, it functions as a fallback option rather than allowing simultaneous use for bonding. To achieve bonding with multiple connections, users must utilize SpeedFusion technology, either through Peplink's service or by hosting a FusionHub. For those needing a dual-modem 5G solution, the BR2 Pro 5G is recommended, while the Max Transit Pro Duo is a solid alternative for users not requiring 5G.

Users can select options such as 'Both SIMs' or force the use of 'SIM A Only' or 'SIM B Only.' In contrast, devices with multiple modems, like the Transit Duo, allow each modem to be listed as a separate WAN connection, enabling users to drag and drop connections and select SIMs for each modem individually.

If this connection is lost during flight, the GPS data cannot be recorded or captured, which poses a significant issue for data correlation with tested locations. This problem appears to have re-emerged in firmware version 8.1.2 GA, despite having been resolved in previous models and firmware updates. A Peplink ticket has been raised to address this issue.

When using the "Both SIMs" setting on a Pepwave device, it attempts to connect using SIM A first, and if that fails, it will switch to SIM B. Conversely, the "Alternate periodically" setting allows for time-based switching between SIMs, which helps to distribute bandwidth usage evenly across both SIMs, especially when there are restrictions on a single SIM's bandwidth allowance.

For a single session from one LAN device to leverage all available WANs simultaneously, SpeedFusion Bonding is required. A practical way to implement SpeedFusion bonding is by using a FusionHub hosted in Vultr for a monthly fee.

The Pepwave MAX BR1 has two SIM card slots but only one cellular modem, meaning it can only use one SIM card at a time, and therefore cannot double speeds. SmartCheck performs health checks on the cellular connection only when there is no active traffic, which helps maintain stability. If the connection goes idle, it will revert to using the DNS servers defined under the WAN Connection Settings.

The Pepwave MAX BR1 has a single modem, which means it cannot route specific traffic types, such as data traffic and VoIP traffic, over different SIM cards. The secondary SIM card is intended for failover and redundancy purposes only.

query: How do the capabilities and constraints of utilizing multiple SIM cards at once in Pepwave MAX BR1 series devices compare to those in dual-modem devices such as the MAX Transit Duo?
answer: Pepwave MAX BR1 series devices, including the BR1 Pro 5G, BR1 Mk2, and Max BR1 LTE, have two SIM card slots but only one cellular modem. This means only one SIM card can be active at any time, and the secondary SIM serves as a backup for failover, not for simultaneous use or bonding. For users requiring simultaneous multi-carrier connectivity or bonding, a dual-modem device is necessary.

## Document_1

When changing the handshake port on a Pepwave MAX hotspot, the new port should take effect immediately after the changes are applied. If the device continues to use the original port for handshaking, it is recommended to open a support ticket for further assistance.

## Document_2

IP Passthrough is a feature supported only in a single cellular model and is not available in the BR2 Pro. This information has been updated to reflect the correct feature availability.

## Document_3

The MAX BR1 and MAX BR2 models support IP passthrough mode for cellular WAN connectivity.

## Document_4

The router installed in a metallic water-proof box outdoors is experiencing high temperatures around 80℃, which exceeds the specified operational temperature range of -40° to 65°C. To mitigate this issue, it is recommended to ventilate the box, potentially using forced air, or relocate the router to a cooler environment, as prolonged exposure to high temperatures can reduce the mean time between failures (MTBF) of the equipment.

## Document_5

To manage access to different SSIDs on a Pepwave Max BR1 5G, you can define a schedule and set that schedule per SSID, allowing you to turn off the personal AP during work hours when the connection is less than ideal.

## Document_6

The Winegard 360+ antenna system is not suitable for use with the Pepwave Max BR1 Pro 5G due to its insufficient number of antenna elements and its design primarily for 4G/LTE frequencies. It is recommended to use a dedicated 5G antenna, such as the Peplink 42G antenna, which is 5G ready and includes GPS and WiFi capabilities for accessing public WiFi networks.

## Document_7

The user is experiencing issues with their Pepwave MAX BR2 PRO router, specifically related to the WAN to LAN port configuration being reset after changing WAN priority settings. This reset occurs after InControl2 updates the router's configuration, which seems to be incorrectly managing the WAN/LAN local port settings. The user notes that this behavior is new and has not occurred in the past, indicating a potential change in how InControl2 interacts with the device settings.

## Document_8

The Pepwave Max Transit Pro does not support traditional GSM cellular voice calls, but it does allow for SMS messaging and VoIP calls over data connections.

## Document_9

The operating temperature range for the Pepwave Max Transit Duo LTEA is between -40°C and +65°C, as specified in the product data sheet. When enclosing the device in a weather-proof box, it may be necessary to consider a case with ventilation depending on the external environment.

## Document_10

Sprint does not activate data plans on commercial router devices like the Pepwave Max Transit LTEA Cat 18. The pricing for data plans on such devices is typically higher than consumer hotspot plans, with costs around $6.00 to $9.00 per gigabyte being more realistic.

## Document_11

PepVPN will continue to function even if PrimeCare is not renewed for a Pepwave MAX Transit CAT 18, although SpeedFusion will not work without an active PrimeCare subscription.

## Document_12

A well-ventilated Pepwave MAX Transit Duo can have a surface temperature of up to 60°C (140°F) when it is busy. Monitoring the temperature through the web UI can provide additional insights into its operating temperature.

## Document_13

The Pepwave MAX Transit models can operate at warmer temperatures, which is normal due to the design where the metal case acts as a heatsink for the internal circuitry. Even in cold environments, the units may feel warm to the touch, indicating typical operational behavior rather than overheating.

## Document_14

The Pepwave MAX BR1 Pro does not support converting the WAN port to a LAN port, which means it cannot be configured to provide additional LAN ports beyond the default number available.

## Document_15

To resolve issues with a Pepwave Max Mobile Router not displaying daily data usage for previous days, it is recommended to check the firmware version and upgrade to the latest firmware if it is not already being used.

## Document_16

For configuring multiple Pepwave Max BR1 devices, the InControl2 cloud management platform can be used to store configurations in the cloud and push them to all devices, facilitating pre-staging of configurations.

## Document_17

The Pepwave Max Transit Cat-18 has been certified for use by Verizon for some time. For updates on 5G devices, it is suggested to contact Peplink directly.

## Document_18

The Cricket plan is compatible with Pepwave Max Transit devices, specifically the Max Transit Duo, providing a potential unlimited data solution for users.

## Document_19

The Cricket unlimited plan is compatible with Pepwave Max Transit devices and has been reported to work as intended by users.

## Document_20

The Pepwave MAX Transit Mini is now certified for use on the Verizon network, indicating compatibility with Verizon SIM cards for authentication.

## Document_21

To use Pepwave Max devices with Google's ProjectFi, it is important to ensure that roaming is enabled in the Peplink settings to avoid any connectivity issues.

## Document_22

When a router is installed in a metallic water-proof box outdoors, it can experience excessive heat, with reported temperatures around 80°C, which exceeds the operational temperature range of -40° to 65°C specified in the data sheet. To mitigate overheating, it is recommended to implement solar shading, add heat sinks, and consider forced air cooling.

## Document_23

There is an issue with the Peplink MAX BR2 PRO where changes to the WAN to LAN port configuration are being reset to default after modifying WAN priority settings. This behavior appears to be linked to InControl2, which is automatically updating configurations and causing the loss of connection. Users have reported that this issue started recently and affects their ability to manage WAN/LAN settings effectively, leading to connectivity problems for multiple devices.

## Document_24

The user experienced issues with their MAX BR2 PRO router where the WAN to LAN configuration was reset to default after changing WAN priority settings. This reset was linked to InControl2 updating the router's configuration automatically, which was not expected as the user had not enabled InControl to manage device-specific port settings. After reconfiguring the WAN to LAN setting, the user noted that the changes remained intact for a period without being overridden by InControl, suggesting a potential temporary resolution to the issue.

## Document_25

The Pepwave Max Transit LTEA Cat 18 is compatible with Sprint, but users may face challenges activating it with certain Sprint hotspot plans. Entering the Max Transit's IMEI on Sprint's activation page may result in an error indicating that the device cannot be activated. Users have expressed concerns about the high cost of data plans for quality routers compared to cheaper hotspot devices, which can lead to frustration, especially in rural areas with limited internet options.

## Document_26

Cricket offers a 100 GB data plan for Pepwave Max Transit Cat 18 devices, priced at $90 per month, along with additional options of 40 GB for $50 and 20 GB for $35. These plans provide high-speed data access for browsing, streaming, and downloads, but do not include calling. Additionally, AT&T offers business data plans with varying speeds and prices: $80/month for 8 Mbps, $130/month for 12 Mbps, $200/month for 50 Mbps, and $300/month for 100 Mbps. These business plans are not intended for streaming video or entertainment, but provide unlimited data capped at the specified plan speed.

## Document_27

To connect a Pepwave BR1 mini to Google's Project Fi, first access the cellular connection settings and ensure the Network Selection is set to Auto. Then, restrict the connection to the carrier by scanning for available networks, where Project Fi should appear alongside others like Sprint and Verizon. In the APN settings, change to custom and input 'h2g2' as the APN to establish the connection successfully.

## Document_28

Using a data-only Project Fi SIM with Pepwave Max devices outside of the US can present challenges, particularly with network recognition and connection stability. Users have reported seeing a 'Project F' network in the US, but this is not available in countries like France or Spain. When attempting to connect, selecting various local carriers such as Free, Vodafone ES, Orange, YOIGO, Movistar, GIBTEL, and Shine has not yielded success, with the connection status often stuck on 'Obtaining IP address'. The antenna status fluctuates between showing strong signal bars and none, indicating potential issues with network compatibility or settings. The device consistently reports the carrier as T-Mobile and the region as the United States, which may affect connectivity.

## Document_29

For using Pepwave Max devices with Google's Project Fi, the correct APN to configure is h2g2. It is also recommended to enable roaming for the BR2 cellular WAN during testing. If connection issues persist despite enabling roaming, it is advised to open a support ticket for further assistance.

## Document_30

Pepwave Max devices can be used with Google's ProjectFi, and it is recommended to set the APN to h2g2. For devices shipped out of the country, it is advisable to activate the SIM card in a US device first to ensure data activation. The BR1 MINI APAC unit is suitable for use in the Philippines, and it is important to check the device's ability for data roaming, as it will automatically select a partner cellular network based on roaming agreements.

## Document_31

When attempting to use Google Fi with a Pepwave BR1 device in Spain, the device shows available networks but fails to connect, getting stuck at 'obtaining DHCP address' despite having the correct APN settings. The same SIM card works correctly in a tablet with the same APN and network, indicating a potential issue specific to the BR1 device.

Dynamic Multipoint VPN (DMVPN) is a proprietary technology developed by Cisco, and as such, it is not available for use by other vendors, including Peplink. Therefore, Peplink products do not support DMVPN unless Cisco decides to license its use to other vendors, which is currently not the case.

The reset button must be held until all lights on the router turn off to ensure a proper factory reset. Additionally, the network cable should be connected to one of the LAN ports, not a WAN port, to establish a connection.

Check the enable box to expand the menu, and input the destination IP address or hostname along with a port number, which can be any number that the server accepts. Choose between UDP or TCP, with UDP being the default. The reporting interval can be set to one second or adjusted to a longer interval, such as five seconds for stationary reporting. query: In what ways does the InControl2 (IC2) management and registration status impact a technician’s capability to access and set up a pre-owned Peplink router following a factory reset, and what measures are necessary to guarantee unrestricted administrative access?
answer: A used Peplink router that is still registered to another user's InControl2 (IC2) account may prevent normal administrative access even after a factory reset. When the router connects to the internet, IC2 can automatically push previous configurations, which may change the admin credentials, IP address, or other settings, making local access difficult or impossible. To ensure full administrative access, the technician should remove all SIM cards and WAN cables before performing a hard reset, then log in using default credentials at the default IP address (commonly 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.50.1). Once logged in, IC2 communication should be disabled in the system settings to prevent further remote configuration. Finally, the technician should contact the previous owner or Peplink support to have the device removed from the former IC2 account, providing proof of ownership if necessary. This process restores full local and cloud management capabilities to the new owner.

citations.claim: A device registered to another user's InControl2 account can block admin access after reset by pushing previous configurations (changing credentials or settings).
After reset, removing all SIM cards and WAN cables prevents new IC2 configurations from being applied during reboot.
Default login credentials and IP addresses (such as 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.50.1) should be used immediately after reset before the device connects to the internet.
Disabling IC2 communication in system settings after login prevents further remote configuration from IC2.
To fully transfer ownership, the device must be removed from the previous IC2 account by contacting the former owner or Peplink support and providing proof of ownership.

The Peplink Balance 380 HW5 has a maximum router throughput of 200Mbps, which is insufficient given the combined WAN speeds of 200Mbps, 150Mbps, and 120Mbps. The device is experiencing saturation at 150Mbps due to its limitations. For improved performance, it is recommended to upgrade to a newer model, such as the Balance 380 HW6, which supports 1Gbps Stateful Firewall Throughput.

## Document_2

The Peplink Balance 20 and 30 routers are limited to approximately 200mb throughput, which creates a bottleneck for users in areas where gigabit download speeds are being rolled out. The current lineup of Peplink routers does not support gigabit throughput until the 300 series and higher. This limitation affects small business and residential users who expect to utilize gigabit service without significant speed loss, as they may experience a 40% drop in speed when using these routers.

## Document_3

A Peplink Balance 20 or 30 can combine both DSL and cable internet connections for load balancing and automatic failover, ensuring continuous connectivity. The AP One access points are suitable for enhancing wireless coverage in larger homes, utilizing TruePower RF technology for increased signal strength. The AP One operates on the 2.4GHz band, while the AP One mini supports 5GHz, which may require compatible devices for optimal performance.

## Document_4

answer: The throughput limitations and hardware revisions of the Peplink Balance 210 and 310 models significantly constrain their ability to utilize the full bandwidth of multiple WAN connections when bonding. The Balance 210 HW4 has a maximum straight WAN routing throughput of 350Mbps, but SpeedFusion VPN throughput is limited to 80Mbps encrypted and 150Mbps unencrypted. Earlier revisions (HW1) are even more limited, with only 50Mbps total router throughput and 30Mbps for encrypted VPN. The Balance 310’s throughput varies by hardware revision: HW1 is capped at 50Mbps, HW3 at 200Mbps, and some sources reference a 100Mbps WAN-to-LAN rating for certain revisions. These limitations mean that when bonding multiple WANs (e.g., three 80Mbps lines), the aggregate speed is still capped by the device’s throughput limit (e.g., 80Mbps for the 210 HW4). For users who require higher aggregate speeds (e.g., to fully utilize gigabit or multiple high-speed WANs), upgrading to newer models such as the Balance 380 HW6 (1Gbps throughput), Balance One/Core (400-600Mbps), or Balance 310 5G (170–240Mbps download) is recommended. These newer models offer significantly higher throughput, better hardware, and support for modern features, enabling users to take full advantage of faster internet connections and advanced bonding capabilities.

In the context of a Pepwave 20X device using Dynamic Weighted Bonding (DWB), it has been observed that even without WAN Smoothing configured, the device shows a consistent low rate of packets being sent for WAN smoothing in the detailed graphs. This behavior is attributed to TCP ACK optimization, which is a feature of DWB. In version 8.2.0, users will have the option to disable TCP ACK optimization if desired.

## Document_2

The issue with the Balance 20X not connecting may be related to a bug that was fixed in firmware version 8.1.1. The response indicates that previous problems associated with connectivity have been resolved in this update, suggesting that users experiencing similar issues should ensure they are running the latest firmware version.

## Document_3

The issue with the Pepwave Sure SOHO MK3's 2.4GHz SSID not allowing certain clients to connect after a period of time may be related to the WiFi connection between the affected clients and the router. While the 2.4GHz SSID is still visible, affected clients cannot connect to it after disconnection, although it reappears after some time. The problem does not affect all wireless clients simultaneously, suggesting it may not be a widespread issue with the MK3's WiFi functionality. Signal strength measurements of the affected clients may provide further insight into the problem.

## Document_4

The Max HotSpot supports Virtual WAN (VWAN) as it is compatible with firmware version 8.3, which includes this feature.

## Document_5

When using a Peplink Balance 20 configured for PPTP, users may connect to the home network and access the router's admin page, but may experience issues connecting to other LAN devices, such as failing to ping them or access services like RDP. This could indicate a need for specific firewall rules to be created, as the existing rules may not apply to PPTP connections as expected, despite the standard rule allowing all outgoing traffic.

## Document_6

When configuring a Peplink Balance 20 for PPTP access, users may encounter issues connecting to other devices on the LAN, despite being able to access the admin page. This may be due to the need for specific firewall rules to be created, as existing rules may not apply to PPTP connections in the same way they do for local connections. Users should ensure that appropriate firewall rules are set to allow traffic from the PPTP VPN to the LAN devices.

## Document_7

When using PPTP on a Peplink Balance 20, users may experience issues accessing local network devices and the internet despite being able to connect to the home network. This could be due to firewall rules that need to be configured, as existing rules may not apply to VPN connections. It is important to ensure that appropriate firewall rules are set to allow traffic from the VPN to local resources and the internet.

## Document_8

The Peplink Balance 380 can successfully maintain L2TP/IPSec connections for over an hour when using firmware version 8.0.0. The user tested the connection with a Windows 10 L2TP/IPSec client without experiencing disconnections, indicating that the issue may not be with the Peplink device itself but potentially with the client's configuration or network environment.

## Document_9

The maximum throughput for PPTP connections on a Peplink Balance 20 is not specified in the conversation. However, it is suggested to check user groups and bandwidth control settings in the configuration, which may affect performance. When upgrading from firmware version 6.3.2 to 7.1.0, the current configuration will be retained, and there is an option to revert to the previous firmware version after the upgrade. Changes made in the newer firmware will not apply to the older version, but configurations can be exported from the newer firmware and imported into the older version if needed.

## Document_10

The Peplink Balance 20 does not impose specific speed limitations on PPTP connections beyond the available bandwidth of the device itself. However, if remote users are connecting from distant locations with many network hops, increased latency can negatively affect the bandwidth available for those PPTP sessions.

## Document_11

The Peplink Balance 710 devices are currently running firmware version 5.2.9. Users may encounter an 'Unlock key validation failed' error when attempting to unlock the device using the serial number found on the chassis. This suggests that the serial number may not be correctly associated with the unlock key, or there may be an issue with the firmware or device configuration.

## Document_12

The Balance 20 is experiencing connectivity issues when its WAN 2 port is connected to a LAN port on a PepWave SOHO, remaining stuck in 'Connecting...' status. The SOHO is configured as a DHCP server, which should provide WAN 2 network parameters to the Balance 20. Both devices are running firmware version 6.3.0. A workaround for a similar issue with a Comcast cable modem involves rebooting the modem, but rebooting the SOHO does not resolve the problem. The SOHO can connect to the Balance 20's LAN port, but this configuration does not meet the user's needs for WiFi connectivity from a Verizon modem.

## Document_13

Random system startups on Pepwave devices such as the Surf Soho, Balance 20, and Balance One may occur after upgrading to firmware version 6.2.1, as reported by users. The issue does not appear to affect models like the 305 and 380, which are running the same firmware. There is no indication in the logs to suggest a specific cause, as the logs only show a generic 'System: Started up' message.

## Document_14

The Peplink Balance units utilize a latency check for outbound traffic by default, which helps in determining the quickest return path for sessions initiated on the network. This feature is available in the current firmware version 6.1.2. Users can also set up additional rules to further shape traffic according to their needs, allowing for more sophisticated management of multiple WAN connections.

## Document_15

To troubleshoot connectivity issues with a PPTP server on a Balance 20, ensure that PPTP clients are configured to use the remote default gateway. Additionally, firewall rules can be implemented on the Balance to control access, allowing only specific protocols or destinations as needed.

## Document_16

The most recent API documentation available for Peplink devices is for firmware version 8.3.0, and there is currently no documentation released for version 8.4.0.

## Document_17

Users experiencing issues with the Pepwave MAX Transit Mini not recognizing the hardwired WAN line and failing to obtain an IP address on cellular may be encountering a firmware-related problem. A temporary fix involves logging into each affected Transit Mini and reverting the firmware to version 8.2.1, as upgrading to version 8.3 can cause these issues. It is also advisable to open a support ticket for further assistance.

## Document_18

There is an issue with receiving SMS messages on a Verizon hotspot SIM in the Pepwave MAX BR1 mini after applying firmware version 8.0.0. The user is unable to receive a temporary code sent by Verizon for account management, which is necessary for logging into their Verizon account. The user also mentions that the SIM card size is incompatible with other devices, preventing them from accessing the SMS messages through an alternate device.

## Document_19

The Pepwave MAX BR1 HW2 with firmware version 7.0 supports load balancing, allowing the use of both a WAN port for fiber broadband and a mobile broadband SIM card concurrently. This setup can provide either failover capabilities or combined speed, depending on the configuration.

## Document_20

With the release of version 7, the PEPWAVE MAX BR1 can support concurrent LTE and Satellite WAN connections. This allows for the creation of two tunnels to utilize each link effectively. Additionally, selected MAX single cellular models now support load balancing and WAN Smoothing, which can help in managing traffic between the data center and private networks.

## Document_21

Firmware version 7 on Pepwave MAX BR1 LTE and BR1 Pro LTE supports the use of the LTE cellular port and the physical WAN port simultaneously as two separate gateways to the LAN. Additionally, selected MAX single cellular models support load balancing and WAN Smoothing, including the BR1, BR1 Slim, BR1 ENT, and Transit models.

## Document_22

The Bonjour Forwarding feature is not available on the Surf SOHO MK3 running firmware version 8.1.0; it is only available on the Balance series of devices. The user also mentions difficulties in getting it to work on a Balance 20X device.

## Document_23

The firmware update check feature on the device may have a delay in reporting the latest available firmware version. Users can manually download the latest firmware version 3.5.4 from the provided URL to update their access points.

## Document_24

Firmware version 6.3.1 is expected to contain a fix for connectivity issues experienced with certain devices on the LAN side of the Pepwave Surf SOHO router after upgrading to firmware 6.3.0, which caused two of the three devices to lose connectivity and not appear on the Status Client List.

## Document_25

To log the URLs visited by each user on Peplink devices as of Firmware 6.3, navigate to Network > Firewall > Content Blocking, enable the feature, and enter the IP address and port of the remote syslog server. The IP address should correspond to the machine running the KIWI software for logging purposes.

## Document_26

The API documentation for Peplink has been fixed and is now accessible at the provided link.

## Document_27

To manage a Starlink dish connected to a Peplink Balance router, it may be necessary to pass through the IP address 192.168.100.1 to WAN1. This can potentially be achieved by adding a Static Route for the 192.168.100.0/24 subnet to the gateway IP of the Starlink interface. Additionally, it is noted that running firmware version 8.1.1 may be required for certain features to function correctly in drop-in mode.

## Document_28

To set up a Peplink Balance 20X with both CenturyLink and Starlink internet connections, the CenturyLink modem should connect to the Peplink via Ethernet, and the Starlink router can also connect to the Peplink using an Ethernet adapter. A USB dongle may be required for the CenturyLink modem connection. The Peplink Balance 20X requires a PrimeCare subscription to maintain SpeedFusion Cloud service, and users can also consider SpeedFusionSolo for potentially lower costs. It is important to keep the PrimeCare subscription active to avoid losing Fusion link functionality. Additionally, users may need to adjust the MTU settings for reliable connections, depending on the internet service used.

## Document_29

In a configuration involving a Peplink 20X connected to a FusionHub (FH) with a profile set for Dynamic Weighted Balancing (DWB), there is an observation of WAN Smoothing being reported in the detailed graphs despite it not being enabled. The graphs show a consistent low rate of packets being sent for WAN smoothing, which raises questions about whether this is a rendering issue or a side effect of the DWB configuration. The expectation is that if WAN smoothing were operational, there would be more balanced traffic across multiple WAN links due to redundant packets being sent and received.

## Document_30

To troubleshoot connectivity issues with the Peplink Balance 20X when using cable internet, it is suggested to consider the network setup, particularly whether the ISP provides a router. In such cases, the ISP's router should be treated as the first router, with the Peplink acting as the second router. This configuration can enhance security by preventing the ISP from accessing detailed network information. The Peplink Balance 20X offers a good level of security out of the box, and additional security layers can be implemented through VLANs and access rules, depending on the complexity of the network environment.

## Document_31

The Balance 20X may experience connectivity issues with certain cable modems, which is a known problem that has not yet been resolved. For initial setup and security configuration, instructions for the Surf SOHO can also be applied to the Balance 20X, as the user interface is mostly similar. Additionally, using a Peplink product is generally more secure than using a standard ISP router or devices like Synology NAS, which prioritize sharing over security.

## Document_32

The Balance 20X may experience connectivity issues with cable internet, potentially due to problems with the ISP, as indicated by packet capture analysis. In a similar case, a user faced connection issues with a Protectli FW4B and resolved the problem by introducing an Asus router between the devices, suggesting that using an additional router may help in troubleshooting connectivity problems with cable modems.

## Document_33

There is a known bug related to connectivity issues with the Peplink Balance 20X that has been previously documented in a forum thread. Troubleshooting efforts may be necessary to resolve the connectivity problems, particularly when using cable internet with Comcast. The specific details of the bug and potential solutions can be found in the referenced thread.

## Document_34

To resolve connectivity issues with the Peplink Balance 20X, it is recommended to follow a specific power cycling protocol: unplug all devices including the modem and router for 20 minutes, then plug in the Balance 20X first and allow it to sit for five minutes before connecting the modem and Cat cable. After this procedure, the device should establish a stable connection. The user reported successful connectivity after applying firmware version 8.1.3 and noted that the connection remained stable for two days without interruption, except when intentionally disconnected.

## Document_35

The Pepwave Sure SOHO MK3 is experiencing connectivity issues with its 2.4 GHz SSID, where devices can connect for a few hours before losing the ability to connect, although the SSID remains visible. The 5 GHz band continues to function without issues. The firmware version 7.1.0 operates correctly, while version 8.0.0 appears to cause connectivity problems after a period of time.

## Document_36

The Pepwave Sure SOHO MK3 is experiencing connectivity issues with the 2.4 GHz SSID, which connects for a few hours before stopping connections, while the 5 GHz SSID remains accessible. The issue appears to be related to firmware version 8.0.0, as the device operates normally on firmware version 7.1.0. The problem may not affect all devices connecting to the 2.4 GHz network, indicating that it could be device-specific.

## Document_37

When using a Peplink Balance 20 configured for PPTP, users may experience issues accessing other devices on the LAN or browsing the internet despite being connected. To resolve this, it is suggested to configure both inbound and outbound firewall rules to Allow All. This should enable access to the LAN once the PPTP connection is established, but additional filtering or blocking on the LAN may also be affecting connectivity.

## Document_38

When configuring a Peplink Balance 20 for PPTP connections, if the remote client cannot connect to other devices on the LAN or browse the internet, it may be due to both the client and the LAN being on the same subnet. Changing the client's IP address to a different subnet, such as 192.168.2.x, could resolve the issue.

## Document_39

When configuring a Peplink Balance 20 for PPTP access, users may encounter issues connecting to other devices on the LAN, despite being able to access the admin page. This could be due to routing configurations, particularly if the local LAN and home LAN share the same subnet, which complicates traffic routing. It is suggested to create static routes on the client device to ensure traffic is directed through the VPN to the home LAN. Additionally, users should verify firewall rules, as they may need to be adjusted to allow traffic from the VPN to the LAN devices.

## Document_40

To enable access to devices on a LAN through a PPTP VPN connection on a Peplink Balance 20, it is necessary to create an inbound firewall rule that allows traffic from the VPN source IP range to the LAN destination IP range. The rule should specify the WAN connection as 'Any', the protocol as 'Any', and set the source and destination IPs and masks to match the LAN addressing. This configuration allows VPN users to access endpoints on the LAN, which may not be accessible by default.

## Document_41

Additionally, enabling InterVlan routing has been suggested as a potential solution, but may not resolve the connectivity issues on its own.

query: What firewall and routing settings must be set up on a Peplink Balance 20 to allow remote clients using PPTP VPN to connect to LAN devices and access the internet, and what typical problems related to subnetting should be taken into account?
answer: To enable remote PPTP VPN clients to access devices on the LAN and internet resources through a Peplink Balance 20, you must create specific firewall rules that allow traffic from the VPN IP range to the LAN IP range. Existing default firewall rules may not apply to PPTP connections, so both inbound and outbound rules permitting all traffic between the VPN and LAN are recommended. Additionally, ensure that the remote client and the LAN are not on the same subnet; if they are, change the client’s subnet (e.g., to 192.168.2.x) to avoid routing conflicts. If necessary, create static routes on the client device to direct traffic for the home LAN through the VPN. Enabling InterVLAN routing may help but is not always sufficient without proper firewall configuration. Finally, confirm that the PPTP client is set to use the remote default gateway to access internet resources through the VPN.

citations.claim: Default firewall rules often do not apply to PPTP connections; specific rules must be created to allow VPN-to-LAN traffic.
Inbound firewall rules should allow traffic from the VPN source IP range to the LAN destination IP range, with protocol and WAN set to 'Any'.
Both inbound and outbound firewall rules should be set to Allow All to enable full access once the PPTP VPN is established.
If the remote client and LAN are on the same subnet, routing issues will prevent access; changing the client’s subnet resolves this.
Creating static routes on the client may be necessary if both subnets overlap, to direct traffic through the VPN to the home LAN.
Enabling InterVLAN routing may help, but is insufficient without proper firewall rules for PPTP traffic.
PPTP clients should be configured to use the remote default gateway to access internet resources via the VPN.

If the client and LAN are on the same subnet, change the client’s subnet (e.g., to 192.168.2.x) to avoid routing conflicts.
If necessary, create static routes on the client device to direct traffic for the home LAN through the VPN.
Enabling InterVLAN routing may help but is not always sufficient without proper firewall configuration.
Confirm that the PPTP client is set to use the remote default gateway to access internet resources through the VPN.

query: What methods, whether remote, local, or hardware-based, are supported for an administrator to restore access to the Web Admin interface of a Pepwave Balance device if they become locked out?
answer:
To regain access to a Pepwave Balance device when locked out of the Web Admin interface, several options are available: 

1. If the device is managed via InControl2 (IC2), use InControl2 to reset or view the admin credentials, or access the remote Web Admin tool to change the password and regain access. 
2. If the device is offline in InControl2, connecting a network cable to the WAN port may bring it back online, enabling remote management. 
3. Locally, pressing and holding the reset button for 5-10 seconds will reset the admin password to the default ('admin') without a full factory reset on most models; holding for 20 seconds will perform a factory reset, erasing all settings. 
4. On Balance 305 and above (from firmware 5.4), the LCD panel can be used to navigate to Maintenance > Reset Admin Password to reset the admin password. 
5. If the reset button is inaccessible, regaining access may only be possible via InControl2, or else a factory reset is necessary if credentials cannot be retrieved. 
6. After a factory reset, the default credentials ('admin'/'admin') can be used to log in. 
7. If a device was previously online with InControl, a saved configuration file may be uploaded to restore settings after reset.

To set up an IPSec VPN between PepLink and Forti, a PDF guide is available that provides detailed instructions for the configuration process.

To create a VPN connection between two Peplink units, specifically the BPL 305 and BPL 310, users can refer to the Balance and MediaFast User Manual for Firmware 7, which is available for download on the Peplink website under the Support section.

## Document_4

To establish a site-to-site VPN between a Peplink-360 and Peplink-310 with a Cisco ASA, it is important to address the double NAT issue and the private IP configuration on the ASA. The peer ID on the Branch Peplink-310 should match the WAN IP of the HQ Peplink-360. The Branch Peplink-310 can operate with a PPPoE dialer and a fixed IP, but it is crucial to determine if aggressive mode is necessary for both the Peplink and Cisco ASA configurations. Creating a SpeedFusion VPN profile between the Peplink devices allows for custom outbound rules to manage traffic across the tunnel effectively.

## Document_5

The conversation discusses a network topology involving a Peplink-360 and Peplink-310 with a Cisco ASA for VPN termination. The HQ Peplink-360 is in VPN passthrough mode with a static IP, while the Branch Peplink-310 uses a PPPoE dialer with a fixed IP. The configuration faces issues due to double NAT and a private IP on the Cisco ASA, which is affecting the peer ID for the VPN connection. The user is exploring aggressive mode for IKE1 on the Peplink-310 and inquiring about the need for similar configuration changes on the Cisco ASA. The conversation suggests that the network design may need reevaluation and mentions the potential use of SpeedFusion VPN for better performance.

## Document_6

The Peplink B-380 and B-580 can serve as routers for outside traffic to different ISPs, support load balancing across three ISP links, and utilize SpeedFusion technology for connecting with remote sites. However, while Peplink appliances are primarily SD-WAN devices with reliable firewall capabilities, they may not fully replace the functionality of existing SRX firewalls. It is recommended to conduct thorough testing and refer to technical documentation for deployment guidance.

## Document_7

The Peplink B-380 can be configured in drop-in mode with a public IP assigned to it. It is possible to configure multiple public IPs from different ISPs on the Peplink B-380, allowing for redundancy in case one ISP link goes down. However, specific details on how to connect to the Peplink from a public network when an ISP is down were not provided in the response.

The Peplink 580 HW1 has a default configuration where the LAN port functions as a trunk port. Users can modify the port settings by navigating to Network > LAN > Port Settings in the device's interface.

To configure a SpeedFusion tunnel from a Peplink PL380A in Layer 3 mode to a PL580, and a second SpeedFusion tunnel in Layer 2 mode from the PL380A to a PL380B, it is necessary to ensure that the IP addressing is correctly set up. For Layer 2 configurations, both sites should not use the same IP address and gateway; instead, they should have distinct gateway IPs, such as 192.168.50.1 for Site 1 and a different address for Site 2, to avoid conflicts and ensure proper routing.

These models support NAT for all WAN ports and can reroute traffic from a congested or failed link to other WAN links with different NAT configurations. However, specific information regarding failover for WAN links and NAT resolution for users when one of the WAN links goes down is not provided.

All versions of the Peplink B310 are compatible with the latest firmware, indicating that there are no limitations on firmware upgrades for this model.

## Document_12

For Peplink B2500, NAT loopback functionality is available without requiring additional configuration, provided that proper inbound NAT rules are defined. This allows devices on the local network to access services using the public IP address of the router.

## Document_13

## Document_14

To enhance WAN capabilities for a branch using a B210, it is recommended to consider a Balance 580 if five WAN connections are needed for internet load balancing. The combination of a B50 with a B210 is not explicitly supported for this purpose, and using multiple devices may complicate the SpeedFusion tunnel setup. There is no mention of a buyback program for upgrading equipment in the provided information.

## Document_15

The Peplink BPL 210 and BPL 30 can establish a site-to-site VPN, indicated by a green VPN icon, allowing successful pings between the routers' LAN IPs. However, issues arise when attempting to ping hosts within the respective networks, suggesting potential configuration problems related to LAN subnets, VLANs, or WAN connections.

## Document_16

For bonding and failover of ISP connections in a data center setup, Peplink devices like the BPL-135 or BPL-2500 can be utilized. query: What steps can a technician take to address double NAT and peer ID challenges when configuring a site-to-site VPN between a Peplink-310 located at a branch (utilizing PPPoE with a static IP) and a Cisco ASA placed behind a Peplink-360 at headquarters operating in VPN passthrough mode, and which alternative VPN solutions or configuration modifications could enhance the stability and efficiency of this network setup?
answer:
To resolve double NAT and peer ID issues in this setup, first ensure that the peer ID on the Branch Peplink-310 is set to match the WAN IP of the HQ Peplink-360, not the private IP of the Cisco ASA. The double NAT occurs because the Cisco ASA is behind the Peplink-360, which is in VPN passthrough mode and assigns a private IP to the ASA. One solution is to configure the Cisco ASA to use its private LAN IP as its WAN IP and set the Peplink-360 as its WAN gateway, letting VPN traffic route correctly and avoiding reconfiguration of remote VPN endpoints. Alternatively, consider obtaining a new WAN IP range and configuring the Peplink-360 in drop-in mode, which would remove double NAT but requires more extensive network changes.

Additionally, using SpeedFusion VPN technology between Peplink devices is recommended over IPSec or traditional VPNs, as SpeedFusion can maintain VPN connections during WAN failures and aggregate bandwidth across multiple WANs, providing better reliability and performance. Custom outbound rules with SpeedFusion can further optimize traffic over the tunnel. However, IPSec VPNs can still be used when interoperability with Cisco ASA is required, but may be more sensitive to NAT and IP addressing challenges.

documents_text:
## Document_1

The Peplink Balance 310X does not support IP passthrough on WAN and cellular according to the firmware version 8.1.3 build 5162.

## Document_2

The Peplink Balance 310X supports IP forwarding on the WAN side. To enable IP forwarding, users need to access the WAN connection settings and click on the question mark icon for guidance on the next steps.

## Document_3

To enable access to network resources for PPTP users on a Peplink 380, it is necessary to create an inbound firewall rule. The source should be set to the internal network, while the destination can be configured based on desired access: for internal network access only, set the destination to the internal network; for internet browsing capability, set the destination to 'Any'.

## Document_4

To enable access to devices on a LAN through a PPTP VPN connection on a Peplink Balance 20, it is necessary to create an inbound firewall rule that allows traffic from the VPN source IP range to the LAN destination IP range. The rule should specify the WAN connection as 'Any', the protocol as 'Any', and set the source and destination IPs and masks to match the LAN addressing. This configuration allows VPN users to access endpoints on the LAN, which may not be accessible by default.

## Document_5

To enable PPTP clients to access internal resources on a Peplink Balance 310, it is necessary to configure an inbound firewall rule. This rule should allow traffic from the internal network to the desired destination, which can either be set to 'Any' for internet browsing or 'Local network' to restrict access to only local resources without internet browsing through the WAN connections.

## Document_6

The Peplink Balance 30 does not have a limit on the number of SIP endpoints that can be registered. If there are issues with registering more than 20 endpoints, it is recommended to capture a diagnostic report from the Balance while the issue occurs and submit it for support review.

## Document_7

After upgrading a Peplink Balance 30 from firmware version 6 to version 8, issues with communication to access points may arise due to changes in VLAN and routing configurations. Performing a factory reset can help resolve potential incompatibilities with the old configuration, potentially restoring functionality with the access points.

## Document_8

To enable full network access for a remote PC connected via L2TP VPN to a Peplink Balance 30, it is necessary to adjust the firewall settings. Specifically, an inbound firewall rule should be created that allows traffic from the VPN source (the LAN subnet) to the destination (the entire LAN or specific devices) with the action set to allow. This rule should be enabled and configured to apply to the WAN connection used for the VPN.

## Document_9

For monitoring a Peplink Balance 580 using Zabbix with SNMP, Peplink provides a Management Information Base (MIB) file for versions 4.x to 5.x, which can be downloaded from their website. However, there is no specific Zabbix template supported by Peplink for this purpose.

## Document_10

To enable a remote host connected via PPTP to access hosts on a local area network (LAN) through a Peplink Balance 20, it is necessary to create an Allow rule in the firewall settings. This rule should have the source set to 'Any', the destination set to 'Network', the protocol set to 'Any', and the action set to 'Allow'. Additionally, ensure that the remote host's PPTP settings include the option 'Use remote gateway for default gateway' to facilitate proper routing. It is also important to check that no local firewalls, such as Windows Firewall, are blocking connectivity from the remote host.

## Document_11

To allow PPTP clients to see all devices on the 192.168.10.0/24 network when connected, an inbound firewall rule should be created on the Peplink Balance. The rule should specify the source as 192.168.10.0/24, the destination as Any, and the action as Allow. This configuration enables PPTP clients to access devices on the network and also allows them to reach the internet without requiring NAT mapping for the PPTP server.

## Document_12

To troubleshoot port forwarding issues on a network with a Balance 20, it is suggested to temporarily reset firewall rules to their default settings, allowing all inbound and outbound traffic. This can help confirm whether the port forwarding configuration is functioning correctly. Additionally, the internal web server is accessible via its local IP address, but the public IP address times out, indicating a potential misconfiguration in the firewall or port forwarding settings.

## Document_13

For successful port forwarding to an internal web server at 192.168.0.249, ensure that the default gateway on the web server is set to the Peplink Balance LAN IP address (192.168.0.4). This configuration is essential for the server to communicate properly with external traffic. Additionally, when using PPTP, if local internet access is lost and visibility to the network past the VPN device is restricted, it may indicate a misconfiguration in the VPN settings or firewall rules that need to be reviewed.

## Document_14

To set up an inbound firewall rule for a Balance 30 PPTP server, create a rule with the following settings: Rule Name as 'PPTP', enable it, set WAN Connection to 'Any', Protocol to 'Any', Source IP & Port to '192.168.1.0' with a mask of '255.255.255.0', and Destination IP & Port to the same '192.168.1.0' with the same mask. Change the source and destination addressing to match your LAN addressing. This configuration allows VPN access to endpoints on the LAN, not just the Balance 30 itself.

## Document_15

The Peplink Balance 580 currently does not support an uninterruptible power supply (UPS). It has a USB interface, but there are no options in the web interface for UPS support. The user mentions using an APC Smart-UPS X LCD 750VA, indicating a specific UPS model that is not compatible with the Peplink 580 due to the lack of a serial interface.

## Document_16

To effectively use the Pepwave MAX 700 for bonding multiple 4G MiFi dongles for live video streaming, a PepLink Load Balancing router is needed at the office or data center for final data transfer. The MAX 700 can be pre-configured for automatic operation, reducing the need for on-site personnel during events. However, the current SpeedFusion technology may not be fully optimized for live streaming applications, as it can be affected by the slowest WAN link, leading to potential delays. The suggestion is made for Peplink to provide application-specific profiles to simplify configuration for users. Additionally, there are concerns about the need for buffering at the data center to manage reassembly delays during streaming.

## Document_17

For live streaming with increased bandwidth, the Pepwave MAX On-The-Go or MAX 700 are suitable mobile routers that provide more bandwidth through multiple sessions or streams and offer instant fail-over between USB modems. To bond multiple USB modems for a single stream, SpeedFusion VPN bonding technology is required, necessitating a second SpeedFusion-enabled device at the headquarters or data center, with the Peplink Balance 380 being a recommended choice for this purpose.

## Document_18

To block a domain for a specific VLAN, you can create firewall access rules in the advanced settings of your router. This involves setting up a new outbound firewall rule with the desired configuration, including specifying the source as the VLAN subnet and the destination as the domain name you wish to block. The action should be set to deny, and event logging can be enabled or disabled as preferred.

## Document_19

The user is experiencing limited wireless bandwidth, with no device exceeding 5Mbps download speed despite having a 32Mbps line and a 5Mbps fiber line connected through a Peplink Balance 310. The setup is in bridge mode, and the user has tested the connection directly through the ATT 32Mbps router, achieving a maximum of 6Mbps. The office environment is large and contains many walls, which may impact wireless signal strength and speed.

## Document_20

To troubleshoot low wireless speeds when using a Peplink Balance 310 with a 32Mbps ATT WAN, it is recommended to connect a laptop directly to the WAN for a speed test, and then connect the WAN to an AP One and test again with the same laptop. This will help measure the effective bandwidth available over Wi-Fi. It is noted that Wi-Fi performance may yield lower speeds due to environmental factors such as walls and the layout of the office space.

## Document_21

Incontrol and InControl2 are distinct platforms, and there is currently no automated method for migrating devices from Incontrol to InControl2; the migration process must be performed manually.

## Document_22

To log outgoing connections through an OfficePoint 400, Event Logging of Firewall rules must be enabled on a Balance router. For improved functionality, it is recommended to upgrade to the AP One series, as the OfficePoint 400 has been obsoleted.

## Document_23

To verify if the Peplink Balance 310X supports IP passthrough on WAN and cellular, it is recommended to enable the Share Drop-In IP feature if there is insufficient public IP availability, such as when using a /30 subnet for the Drop-in WAN. Non Drop-in WANs also support /30 subnets without issues.

## Document_24

When using a Peplink Balance 20 configured for PPTP, users may experience issues accessing other devices on the LAN or browsing the internet despite being connected. To resolve this, it is suggested to configure both inbound and outbound firewall rules to Allow All. This should enable access to the LAN once the PPTP connection is established, but additional filtering or blocking on the LAN may also be affecting connectivity.

## Document_25

When configuring a Peplink Balance 20 for PPTP connections, if the remote client cannot connect to other devices on the LAN or browse the internet, it may be due to both the client and the LAN being on the same subnet. Changing the client's IP address to a different subnet, such as 192.168.2.x, could resolve the issue.

## Document_26

When configuring a Peplink Balance 20 for PPTP access, users may encounter issues connecting to other devices on the LAN, despite being able to access the admin page. This could be due to routing configurations, particularly if the local LAN and home LAN share the same subnet, which complicates traffic routing. It is suggested to create static routes on the client device to ensure traffic is directed through the VPN to the home LAN. Additionally, users should verify firewall rules, as they may need to be adjusted to allow traffic from the VPN to the LAN devices.

## Document_27

When using a Peplink Balance 20 configured for PPTP, users may connect to the home network and access the router's admin page, but may experience issues connecting to other LAN devices, such as failing to ping them or access services like RDP. This could indicate a need for specific firewall rules to be created, as the existing rules may not apply to PPTP connections as expected, despite the standard rule allowing all outgoing traffic.

## Document_28

When configuring a Peplink Balance 20 for PPTP access, users may encounter issues connecting to other devices on the LAN, despite being able to access the admin page. This may be due to the need for specific firewall rules to be created, as existing rules may not apply to PPTP connections in the same way they do for local connections. Users should ensure that appropriate firewall rules are set to allow traffic from the PPTP VPN to the LAN devices.

## Document_29

When using PPTP on a Peplink Balance 20, users may experience issues accessing local network devices and the internet despite being able to connect to the home network. This could be due to firewall rules that need to be configured, as existing rules may not apply to VPN connections. It is important to ensure that appropriate firewall rules are set to allow traffic from the VPN to local resources and the internet.

## Document_30

When configuring a Peplink Balance 20 for PPTP connections, users may encounter issues accessing other devices on the LAN, despite being able to connect to the home network and the admin page. This could be due to the need for specific firewall rules to be created, as existing rules may not apply to PPTP connections. Additionally, enabling InterVlan routing has been suggested as a potential solution, but may not resolve the connectivity issues on its own.

## Document_31

When using L2TP VPN on a Peplink Balance 30, it is normal for the remote PC to initially appear isolated from the rest of the network, indicated by a padlock icon. To enable access to the entire network from the remote PC, it is important to review the Internal Network Firewall Rules in the admin panel and ensure that there are no Deny rules that could be blocking access.

## Document_32

To stream live video using the MAX 700 by bonding multiple 4G MiFi dongles, a Peplink router is required at the office or datacenter to terminate the SpeedFusion bonded VPN. This router can be pre-configured for automatic operation, eliminating the need for a person to monitor it during events. Compatibility with specific modems like the Huawei E303 USB Modem or the Huawei E586 MiFi Dongle may require additional support, and remote assistance can be enabled for driver development if the modems are not currently supported.

## Document_33

The MAX 700 can bond up to 4 USB dongles for streaming live video, and an additional Wi-Fi connection can be used as a WAN to achieve a total of 5 connections. For optimal performance, having a PepLink Load Balancing router at the office or data center is recommended to manage the final upload. The router can be pre-configured for automatic operation, eliminating the need for constant monitoring during events.

query: Which firewall rule settings must be applied on Peplink Balance 20 and Balance 30 routers to allow a remote PPTP or L2TP VPN client to reach all LAN devices and use the internet, and what are some typical problems that could block this connectivity?
answer: To allow a remote PPTP or L2TP VPN client to access all LAN devices and browse the internet on Peplink Balance 20 and Balance 30, you must create inbound firewall rules that explicitly allow traffic from the VPN source (the PPTP or L2TP subnet) to the LAN subnet. The rule should apply to the WAN connection used for the VPN, with protocol set to 'Any', and both source and destination IP ranges matching the LAN addressing. Common issues that can prevent access include missing or misconfigured firewall rules, overlapping subnets between client and LAN, and the default rules not applying to VPN connections as expected.

query: Which factors could cause a Pepwave Max BR1 Mini to have much lower speeds compared to a mobile hotspot or smartphone with the identical SIM card, and what troubleshooting measures can be used to resolve these problems?
answer: The Pepwave Max BR1 Mini can experience slower speeds than a mobile hotspot or smartphone using the same SIM card due to several factors: (1) carrier throttling or plan limitations when a SIM is used in a commercial router, (2) the hardware limitations of the BR1 Mini, particularly if it is a Cat 4 modem without carrier aggregation, (3) suboptimal cellular signal quality or band selection, (4) configuration or antenna issues, and (5) Wi-Fi performance constraints. To address these issues, first verify with your carrier if your plan is being throttled or is not intended for router use. Next, ensure you are using a BR1 Mini model that supports higher categories and carrier aggregation (such as Cat 6 or Cat 7, if available). Check and improve your cellular signal by repositioning the device or antennas, or by using an external high-gain antenna like the Puma 221. Cycle through available cellular bands by setting the device to Custom band selection rather than Auto. Lastly, make sure both cellular and diversity antennas are properly attached, and consider using Ethernet instead of Wi-Fi if possible to overcome wireless limitations.

answer: The MAX BR1 Pro 5G is a single-modem device using either a Qualcomm X55 or X62 modem, supporting 5G and Wi-Fi 6, with three Ethernet ports (including a 2.5 Gbps port assignable as LAN or WAN), and can achieve up to 400 Mbps via SpeedFusion. It uses two nano SIM slots (one active at a time), supports 4x4 MIMO, and is more affordable, but provides less redundancy than dual-modem routers. In contrast, the MAX BR2 Pro 5G features dual 5G modems (initially X55, updated to X62 in newer models), allowing simultaneous connections to multiple carriers for advanced aggregation, and supports up to seven WAN connections (including two 2.5 Gbps WAN ports, four gigabit LAN ports, and USB tethering). It has four nano SIM slots, supports eSIM, and is built for rugged environments (vehicles, boats), with a wide DC power range and ignition sense. The X62 modem in the updated BR2 Pro 5G supports AT&T's Andromeda Spectrum and more 5G bands, making it more future-proof for AT&T mid-band 5G than the X55-based models, which may not support future AT&T upgrades. For users needing robust, multi-carrier aggregation and operation in demanding mobile scenarios, the BR2 Pro 5G's dual modems and rugged features offer superior flexibility, redundancy, and long-term compatibility, especially for AT&T users or those needing maximum WAN diversity.

Configuring high availability (HA) with two Peplink Balance 580 units that have different hardware versions and firmware (5.4.7 and 5.4.9) is likely to result in failure, as there may be issues with the switching process between Master and Slave. For optimal performance and reliability in HA configurations, it is recommended to use units that are the same model and firmware version.

The Peplink Balance 580 has three hardware revisions (HW). For optimal High Availability (HA) pairing, it is recommended to use either a pair of Balance 580 with HW1, which supports firmware version 6.3.4, or a pair with HW2/3, which supports firmware version 7.0.1. Mixing these two options requires using the latest firmware supported by both units, which is 6.3.4. Performance improvements are noted in the newer hardware platforms, indicating potential performance differences in a production environment when using different hardware versions in an HA setup. Additionally, Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) features are not available on older hardware versions, but HA will function if these features are not enabled.

## Document_4

For the PEPLINK 580, if the hardware revision is 1, it is possible to upgrade directly to firmware version 6.3.4. For hardware revisions 2-3, the direct upgrade is to firmware version 7.0.1. Users can determine their hardware revision by checking specific documentation provided in the forum.

## Document_5

In a Peplink 380 setup with two WAN links, when using drop-in mode for the primary internet link (WAN 3), no additional configuration is required for inbound services to function. However, for the secondary internet link (WAN 2) operating in NAT mode, NAT mapping or inbound services must be configured to correspond with the outside IP addresses of the firewall for proper incoming traffic to internal servers.

## Document_6

It is not possible to align both appliances to the same firmware version due to these limitations. However, it is possible to upgrade from firmware 6.3.1 directly to 7.1.2, and users are encouraged to use the latest firmware version available, which is 7.1.2.

Upgrading a Peplink device with different hardware revisions to different firmware versions (7.1.1 for the slave unit and 6.3.4 for the master unit) is not supported for High Availability (HA) configurations. A hardware refreshment for the old device is recommended to ensure compatibility.

When using a Peplink 580 with three ISPs each providing 10Mbps, WAN aggregation allows for multi-session traffic to achieve a combined speed of up to 30Mbps. However, issues arise when attempting to ping hosts within the respective networks, suggesting potential configuration problems related to LAN subnets, VLANs, or WAN connections.

The IC2 system is responsible for processing configuration requests and pushing updates, which typically occurs within a minute, depending on system load. answer: Setting up High Availability (HA) between two Peplink Balance 580 units with different hardware revisions and firmware versions is technically possible, but it is not recommended and introduces several limitations. Both units must run the same firmware version for reliable HA operation, but the latest firmware versions differ by hardware revision (HW1 supports up to 6.3.4, HW2/3 supports up to 7.0.1 or 7.1.1). The only compatible firmware across all Balance 580 hardware revisions is 6.3.4, and using different firmware versions is unsupported for HA. Performance may be reduced when mixing hardware revisions due to differences in throughput, and some features, such as LACP, are not available on older hardware. For optimal HA performance and compatibility, both units should be the same hardware revision running the same latest firmware. If this is not possible, a hardware refresh is recommended.

## Document_2

The Balance 20 router has a maximum throughput of 150Mbps, which can be exceeded by a 500Mbps WAN connection, potentially leading to performance issues such as high CPU usage and unresponsiveness during large downloads. Users have reported that actual throughput under real-world conditions can be significantly lower than the advertised specifications, with some suggesting that actual throughput may be about one-third of the raw throughput under ideal conditions. query: Which issues might lead the Peplink Balance One/Core router to provide much less than its 600Mbps advertised throughput, and what methods can be used to diagnose and resolve these performance problems?
answer: The Peplink Balance One/Core router, while rated for up to 600Mbps throughput, often delivers significantly lower real-world speeds due to several factors. High CPU usage (often reaching 100% during speed tests) is a major contributor, especially when bandwidth exceeds 300Mbps. Quality of Service (QoS) settings, particularly those prioritizing specific applications, can halve available bandwidth. The firmware version can also impact performance, as some updates introduce features or changes that reduce throughput. Other contributing factors include the number of firewall and outbound rules, VLAN tagging, and the use of PPPoE. The method and environment of speed testing (such as browser choice and whether the router admin page is open during tests) also affect results. To restore expected performance, users should disable or carefully configure QoS, reduce unnecessary firewall/outbound rules, try different firmware versions (including downgrading or factory resetting after an upgrade), use recommended browsers and speed test settings, and ensure environmental factors are optimal. If issues persist, a support ticket with Peplink is advised.

The video discusses the differences between the Starlink standard dish and the Starlink mini dish, both of which are designed for low earth orbit satellite broadband internet. The mini is smaller, lighter, and more portable, making it easier to install and use in remote locations. Both dishes have eliminated the need for a motor, reducing costs and power consumption, with the mini using about half the power of the standard dish. decomposed_answer: A Pepwave router should be used as the central network hub to maximize performance and reliability of a Starlink Mini system in a mobile setting like an RV or boat.
The Starlink Mini’s built-in Wi-Fi 5 router has a limited range of about 1,200 square feet.
The Starlink Mini’s built-in router is susceptible to performance drops in obstructive environments, such as metal vehicles.
The Mini should be connected via Ethernet to a Pepwave router for improved connectivity and speed.
The Pepwave router can combine (bond) Starlink with cellular connections for enhanced redundancy and overall bandwidth.
Configuring the Mini to connect to the Pepwave router puts it into bypass mode.
A reset is required to revert the Mini to internal Wi-Fi after using the Pepwave router in bypass mode.
Powering the Mini requires attention to voltage drop over cable runs.
A 48V supply is recommended to power the Mini over longer cable distances.
Power over Ethernet (PoE) solutions are being developed to simplify the Mini’s installation.
Current setups require care to ensure sufficient voltage at the Starlink Mini dish.
The Pepwave router operates on DC power.
Operating the Pepwave router on DC reduces the number of required power sources compared to the Mini’s power draw.
Integrating both the Mini and cellular WAN sources through the Pepwave router ensures uninterrupted internet access even if the satellite link is temporarily lost.
Data plans that allow in-motion operation should be chosen for optimal mobile use of the Starlink Mini.
Starlink’s mobile priority plans are available for the Mini and can be considered for better service.

query: What factors could cause a Pepwave MAX Transit Mini to consistently provide slower speeds compared to smartphones or more advanced Pepwave devices on the same cellular network under similar conditions, and what solutions are advised for users who require improved performance?
answer: The Pepwave MAX Transit Mini often delivers slower speeds than smartphones or higher-end Pepwave models due to several hardware limitations. It is equipped with a CAT4 modem, which does not support advanced features like carrier aggregation and higher-order modulation found in more recent modem categories. As a result, its maximum router throughput is capped at 100 Mbps, and its cellular performance is generally inferior to that of smartphones and newer routers equipped with CAT6, CAT12, or CAT18 modems. The Mini also only operates on 2.4GHz WiFi, further limiting its wireless performance. Additionally, the device’s hardware may not keep up with the demands of modern networks, and its single-band WiFi without MIMO reduces WiFi-WAN and access point efficiency. For users requiring higher speeds or better reliability, it is recommended to upgrade to devices such as the MAX Transit (CAT12 or CAT18), MAX Transit Duo, Max BR1 Pro 5G, or use a separate device for WiFi access point functions. External antennas may also help if poor reception is a contributing factor.

When Pepwave MAX BR1 units show as offline in InControl despite functioning properly on the client side, it may be due to DNS configuration issues. query: What steps should a technician take to troubleshoot when MAX BR1 devices show as offline in InControl2 but function properly on-site, taking into account both device-side and network-side issues?
answer: When MAX BR1 units show as offline in InControl2 but operate normally from the local perspective, technicians should follow a multi-layered troubleshooting approach. First, verify that the device's InControl2 subscription or warranty is active, as connectivity may be affected if these have lapsed. Next, check if the required ports (UDP 5246 and TCP 443/5246) are open and not blocked by the ISP, since access to InControl2 servers depends on these being available. Intermittent ISP port blocking can also cause such issues, so confirm port access from the client side. Investigate DNS configuration: ensure that DNS filtering is not preventing the device from resolving InControl2 servers and, if necessary, switch to a reliable DNS service (such as Google DNS). If all network settings are correct and the issue persists, resetting the device to factory settings can temporarily restore connectivity, indicating a network-level problem rather than a device fault. Finally, if issues continue after these checks, open a support ticket with Peplink and enable Remote Access for further diagnostics.

The Pepwave Transit Duo can be powered using a Micro USB supplying 5V at 2A or through a DC input ranging from 12 to 48V DC at 2A, which can be connected via the terminal block or barrel socket.

To factory reset a Pepwave MAX BR1 Mini LETA router, insert a paperclip into the reset button on the front of the unit and hold it for 10 seconds.

The Winegard 360+ antenna system is not suitable for use with the Pepwave Max BR1 Pro 5G due to its insufficient number of antenna elements and its design primarily for 4G/LTE frequencies. For repair and replacement parts for broken antennas on a Pepwave device, it is recommended to log a ticket with engineering for assistance with RMA and repair services.

The Pepwave MAX BR1 Pro does not support converting the WAN port to a LAN port, which means it cannot be configured to provide additional LAN ports beyond the default number available.

When a Pepwave BR1 modem is stuck on 'obtaining IP address' with a Verizon SIM card, it may indicate an issue with the modem's configuration or connectivity. The presence of a purple triangle suggests a warning or error state. Troubleshooting steps include connecting the BR1 to an alternate internet source via Ethernet or Wi-Fi to facilitate remote access for further diagnosis.

The terminal blocks on the device are designed for directly connected power only and do not include a timer function or ignition switch sensing. The Pepwave Transit devices have 5V inputs that allow them to be powered by portable battery packs, requiring a 2A input for proper operation. Users can connect two battery packs to extend the operational time significantly.

The Pepwave Surf SOHO model has a supplied power pack with a current specification of 1.5A, while the newer SOHO MK3 model has an increased power input specification of 3A due to the introduction of dual radio 802.11ac technology.

The AP One Rugged access point features three RP-SMA connectors that are male, which requires antennas with female connectors for proper connection. The included antennas having male connectors indicates a mismatch, suggesting that incorrect antennas were shipped with the device.

## Document_26

The SIM Injector can power up from a 12V source, but it will not provide Power over Ethernet (PoE) output at that voltage. For PoE functionality, it is recommended to connect the SIM Injector to a power source between 48-56V, with 56V being the preferred option for optimal performance.
